1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# PreToolUse:Bash Safety Hook — Block Destructive Commands (v1.38.0)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# Blocks dangerous patterns and suggests safer alternatives.
     6	# Exit 0 = allow, Exit 2 = block (stderr message fed back to agent).
     7	#
     8	# Cycle-111 (sprint-164, 2026-05-16) — ports Anthropic DCG public pattern
     9	# set inline. Source: github.com/anthropics/destructive-command-guard
    10	# Pattern port reference SHA: HEAD as of 2026-05-16 (no specific commit
    11	# pin available — DCG ships rule packs, not single-file source).
    12	# REVIEW-BY: 2026-08-16 — re-sync against upstream DCG every quarter.
    13	#
    14	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — this hook must never fail closed.
    15	# A grep or jq failure must result in exit 0 (allow), not an error.
    16	#
    17	# WHY fail-open (not fail-closed): A safety hook that crashes or encounters
    18	# a parse error must NOT block the agent from operating. The alternative —
    19	# fail-closed — would make jq/grep bugs into denial-of-service attacks
    20	# against the agent. Fail-open with logging is the standard pattern for
    21	# inline security hooks (cf. ModSecurity DetectionOnly mode).
    22	# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix)
    23	#
    24	# WHY GNU/BSD ERE (NOT strict POSIX): grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension not
    25	# available on macOS/BSD or minimal containers. grep -E (Extended Regex)
    26	# with `\s`, `\S`, `\b` extensions works on both GNU grep (Linux) and BSD
    27	# grep (macOS Sonoma+). Strict-POSIX ERE (busybox without -E extensions)
    28	# is NOT in scope per cycle-111 SDD §5.0 honest-scope decision.
    29	# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix; cycle-111 SDD §5.0)
    30	#
    31	# WHY single script for all patterns: NFR-5 single-file invariant. Multiple
    32	# hooks would each read stdin, parse JSON, and run regex — multiplying
    33	# latency per command. A single emit_block helper with sequential patterns
    34	# is simpler and faster. (cycle-111 SDD §5/§6.)
    35	#
    36	# Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111 SDD §11): this hook is a fence
    37	# against routine destructive-command mistakes by autonomous agents, NOT
    38	# a hardened security boundary against intentional bypass. Known accepted
    39	# bypass classes: newline statement separators, subshell wrapping
    40	# (`bash -c '...'`, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing
    41	# WHERE, jq absent from PATH. See SDD §11 for full table.
    42	# Current executable limit examples and issue dispositions:
    43	# docs/runbooks/hook-safety.md (#1047, #1245, #1088, #1031).
    44	#
    45	# cycle-125 FR-1 (2026-09-23) — precision pass against the fleet corpus
    46	# (tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/, replayed by tests/unit/block-destructive-
    47	# bash.bats). Relaxations, each on a positively established predicate:
    48	# FR-2 cache/build vocabulary by last segment, bare names after a
    49	# statement-initial `cd <temp>`, paths strictly below /tmp|/var/tmp|
    50	# /private/tmp, `$TMPDIR/<name>` only with a real temp TMPDIR, a variable
    51	# bound exactly once to `$(mktemp -d)`; FR-1.1 branches that are ancestors
    52	# of main/master (offline `git merge-base`); FR-1.3 generated paths;
    53	# FR-1.4/5/6 only when a SQL runner (psql, mysql, sqlite3, prisma, …) or an
    54	# inline interpreter program (`python -c`, `node -e`) is in the command.
    55	# ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (deliberately not relaxed):
    56	#   * Remote payloads: `ssh host 'rm -rf /'`, `docker exec c rm -rf /data`,
    57	#     `kubectl exec p -- rm -rf /` keep blocking. A scrub of quoted remote
    58	#     payloads was withdrawn at design time (Flatline SKP-001) — the text
    59	#     fence cannot tell a remote target from a local one, and the blast
    60	#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
    61	#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
    62	#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
    63	#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
    64	#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
    65	#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
    66	#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
    67	#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
    68	#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
    69	#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
    70	#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
    71	#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
    72	#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
    73	#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
    74	#
    75	# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
    76	# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
    77	# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
    78	# =============================================================================
    79	# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
    80	# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
    81	# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
    82	# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
    83	# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
    84	# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
    85	# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
    86	# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
    87	# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
    88	# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
    89	# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
    90	# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
    91	# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
    92	# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
    93	# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
    94	# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
    95	# =============================================================================
    96	# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
    97	# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
    98	# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
    99	# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
   100	# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
   101	# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
   102	# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
   103	# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
   104	# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
   105	# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
   106	# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
   107	# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
   108	# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
   109	# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
   110	# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
   111	# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
   112	# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
   113	# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
   114	# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
   115	# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
   116	# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
   117	# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
   118	# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
   119	# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
   120	# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
   121	# =============================================================================
   122	
   123	# =============================================================================
   124	# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
   125	# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
   126	# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
   127	# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
   128	# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
   129	#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
   130	#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
   131	# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
   132	# under a caller's `set -u`.
   133	#
   134	# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
   135	# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
   136	# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
   137	# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
   138	# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
   139	# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
   140	# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
   141	# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
   142	# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
   143	#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
   144	#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
   145	#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
   146	#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
   147	#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
   148	#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
   149	#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
   150	#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
   151	#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
   152	#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
   153	#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
   154	#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
   155	#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
   156	#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
   157	#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
   158	#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
   159	#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
   160	#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
   161	#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
   162	#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
   163	#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
   164	#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
   165	#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
   166	#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
   167	#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
   168	#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
   169	#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
   170	#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
   171	#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
   172	#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
   173	#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
   174	#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
   175	# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
   176	# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
   177	# =============================================================================
   178	_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
   179	_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
   180	_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
   181	_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
   182	_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
   183	_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
   184	_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
   185	_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
   186	_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
   187	_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
   188	_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'

   190	_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'

   197	# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
   198	_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
   199	  case "$1" in
   200	    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
   201	    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;

   203	  esac
   204	  return 1
   205	}
   206	# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
   207	_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
   208	  case "$1" in
   209	    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;

   213	# Command words the fence's own rules match.
   214	_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
   215	  case "$1" in
   216	    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
   217	    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
   218	  esac
   219	  return 1

   221	# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
   222	_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
   223	  case "$1" in
   224	    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;

   229	# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
   230	# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
   231	# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
   232	_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
   233	  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
   234	  n=${#s}
   235	  _bdb_hd_tok=()
   236	  while (( i < n )); do
   237	    ch="${s:i:1}"
   238	    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
   239	      tok="$tok$ch"
   240	      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
   241	        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
   242	      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
   243	        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
   244	        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
   245	      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
   246	        q=""
   247	      fi
   248	      i=$((i + 1)); continue
   249	    fi
   250	    case "$ch" in
   251	      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
   252	      '\')
   253	        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
   254	        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
   255	      ' '|$'\t')
   256	        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
   257	        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
   258	      '#')
   259	        (( have )) || return 1
   260	        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
   261	      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
   262	        op=""
   263	        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
   264	          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
   265	        done
   266	        i=$((i + ${#op}))
   267	        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
   268	          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
   269	        fi
   270	        if (( have )); then
   271	          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
   272	            op="$tok$op"
   273	          else
   274	            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
   275	          fi
   276	          tok=""; have=0
   277	        fi
   278	        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
   279	      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
   280	    esac
   281	  done
   282	  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
   283	  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
   284	  return 0
   285	}

   287	# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an

   289	_bdb_hd_unq_path() {

   301	# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
   302	# content (or cannot be judged).
   303	_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
   304	  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs

   306	    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;

   322	  done

   335	    t="${toks[i]}"
   336	    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
   337	      case "$t" in
   338	        *'<<<') return ;;
   339	        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;

   344	          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
   345	          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
   346	          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
   347	          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
   348	          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))

   350	        *) return ;;
   351	      esac
   352	    fi
   353	    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
   354	  done
   355	  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
   356	  a0="${argv[0]}"
   357	  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"

   362	    t="${argv[i]}"

   366	    cat)

   372	          -a|--append|-p) ;;

   374	          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }

   376	        esac

   378	    echo|printf)

   381	      done ;;

   384	        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
   385	        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;

   387	      esac
   388	      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
   389	        t="${argv[i]}"

   391	          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
   392	          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
   393	          -*)

   395	              i=$((i + 1))

   397	            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
   398	              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
   399	            fi ;;
   400	          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;

   231	# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.

   536	# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,

   572	# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
   573	# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
   574	# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
   575	# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).

   605	# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
     4	# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
     5	# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
     6	# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
     7	#
     8	#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
     9	#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
    10	#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
    11	#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
    12	#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
    13	#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
    14	#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
    15	#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
    16	#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
    17	#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
    18	#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
    19	#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
    20	#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
    21	#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
    22	#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
    23	#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
    24	#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
    25	#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
    26	#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
    27	#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
    28	#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
    29	#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
    30	#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
    31	#       Run state, first match wins:
    32	#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
    33	#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
    34	#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
    35	#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
    36	#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
    37	#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
    38	#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
    39	#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
    40	#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
    41	#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
    42	#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
    43	#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
    44	#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
    45	#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
    46	#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
    47	#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
    48	#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
    49	#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
    50	#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
    51	#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
    52	#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
    53	#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
    54	#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
    55	#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
    56	#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
    57	#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
    58	#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
    59	#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
    60	#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
    61	#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
    62	#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
    63	#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
    64	#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
    65	#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
    66	#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]

    68	#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
    69	#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
    70	#

    72	# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
    73	# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
    74	# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),

    77	# =============================================================================
    78	set -euo pipefail
    79	export LC_ALL=C
    80	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    81	VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
    82	usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    83	
    84	sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
    85	file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
    86	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    87	  case "$1" in
    88	    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    89	    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    90	    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    91	    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    92	    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    93	    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    94	    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    95	    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    96	    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;

   102	
   103	# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
   104	# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
   105	# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
   106	if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then

   109	  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

   118	[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"

   121	now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }
   122	
   123	# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
   124	# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
   125	cfg() {
   126	  local v
   127	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
   128	    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
   129	    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
   130	  else
   131	    printf 'null'
   132	  fi

   134	cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT

   138	
   139	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

   141	# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
   142	# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
   143	# previous file is untouched.
   144	atomic_update() {
   145	  local f="$1"; shift
   146	  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
   147	  (
   148	    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
   149	    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
   150	    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
   151	    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
   152	      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
   153	    else
   154	      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
   155	    fi
   156	    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
   157	    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
   158	  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
   159	  return $rc
   160	}
   161	
   162	cmd_write() {
   163	  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
   164	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi

   166	  ts=$(now_iso)
   167	  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
   168	    '.schema_version = 2
   169	     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
   170	     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?

   173	  local err drc=0

   175	  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi

   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi

   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)

   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'

   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# implement-gate.sh — Dual-mode compliance hook for App Zone writes (FR-7)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# Checks whether Write/Edit to App Zone files occurs within an active
     6	# /implement or /bug skill invocation.
     7	#
     8	# Two detection modes:
     9	#   1. HEURISTIC (ADVISORY, the default): reads .run/ state files for RUNNING state
    10	#   2. AUTHORITATIVE: reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin, only when
    11	#      .loa.config.yaml sets implement_gate.mode: authoritative. The PreToolUse
    12	#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
    13	#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this mode.
    14	#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
    15	#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
    16	#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
    17	#      non-implementation skill asks and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
    18	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
    19	#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask" for a non-implementation
    20	#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
    21	#
    22	# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
    23	# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
    24	# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
    25	#
    26	# Failure mode: FAIL-ASK for App Zone writes (not fail-open). A payload jq cannot
    27	# parse (or no jq), or a file_path that cannot be canonicalised, asks too (run-2
    28	# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
    29	# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
    30	# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
    31	# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
    32	# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location
    33	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
    34	# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
    35	# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
    36	# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl or
    37	# .loa.config.yaml asks and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
    38	# Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.
    39	#
    40	# Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent
    41	# exit 0 with empty stdout; ask = exit 0 with
    42	#   {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}
    43	# A top-level "decision" accepts approve|block only, so "ask" never goes there.
    44	# file_path and active_skill reach stderr only through strip_controls (n21;
    45	# run-2 findings 3/12; run-3 finding 5): cut to 256 bytes without splitting a
    46	# character, then C0 and DEL, UTF-8 C1 controls and the Unicode format/bidi/tag
    47	# code points are removed to a fixed point. Audit rows record the RAW values cut
    48	# the same way and written with jq -a, so every non-ASCII code point is \uXXXX:
    49	# faithful (implement+U+200B logs as implement\u200b) and terminal-safe (run-3 finding 4).
    50	#
    51	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — hook must never crash-block.
    52	# Parse/read errors on App Zone writes → ask (not allow).
    53	#
    54	# Part of cycle-049/050: Upstream Platform Alignment (FR-7)
    55	# Red Team findings addressed: ATK-005 (state tampering), ATK-006 (fail-open),
    56	#   ATK-007 (prompt injection via file path)
    57	# Sprint-108 T4.4: Dual-mode (authoritative + heuristic)
    58	# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization

    60	
    61	# Read tool input from stdin
    62	input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
    63	
    64	# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only

    66	emit_ask() {
    67	    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    68	        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    69	    else
    70	        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
    71	    fi
    72	}
    73	
    74	# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
    75	# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
    76	# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
    77	# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
    78	# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
    79	_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
    80	_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
    81	    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
    82	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
    83	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    84	    done
    85	    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
    86	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    87	    done
    88	    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
    89	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    90	    done
    91	    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
    92	        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    93	    done
    94	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
    95	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    96	    done
    97	    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
    98	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    99	    done
   100	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
   101	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   102	    done
   103	}
   104	
   105	# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
   106	# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
   107	# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
   108	cut_utf8_256() {
   109	    local LC_ALL=C
   110	    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
   111	    _c_n=${#_c_s}
   112	    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
   113	        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
   114	        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
   115	        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
   116	        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
   117	        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
   118	        fi
   119	        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
   120	        return 0
   121	    done
   122	    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
   123	}
   124	
   125	# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
   126	# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting

   128	strip_controls() {
   129	    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq
   130	    cut_utf8_256 s "$1"
   131	    s=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')

   134	        prev=$s
   135	        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done

   141	# The root never follows the process cwd, which follows Claude's `cd` (sprint-250 audit MED-001): PROJECT_ROOT, then

   190	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   203	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   204	# Lexical normaliser for an absolute path: drops empty and . components, resolves .. textually, follows no symlink
   205	_ig_lexical_norm() {
   206	    local rest=$1 part
   207	    local -a out=()
   208	    while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
   209	        part=${rest%%/*}

   212	            ''|.) ;;

   216	    done

   218	    printf '/%s' "${out[*]}"
   219	}

   221	# $1 relative to the root $2, or failure when $1 is not under $2
   222	_ig_under_root() {

   227	canonical_root=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || canonical_root=""

   400	        fi

   418	        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1

   422	        fi
   423	    fi

   425	    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
   426	    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
   427	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then

   432	            return 0
   433	        fi
   434	    fi
   435	
   436	    return 1
   437	}

   440	# Decision: allow or ask

   352	  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '

   380	      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));

   382	      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A

   398	    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")

   401	  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
   402	  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
   403	  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
   404	  rounds="[]"
   405	  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
   406	    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
   407	  fi
   408	  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
   409	    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
   410	  fi
   411	  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
   412	  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
   413	  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
   414	  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
   415	
   416	  local facts report
   417	  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
   418	    {sprints: $s,
   419	     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),

   423	     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')

   425	                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
   426	                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
   427	    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
   428	    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
   429	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
   430	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
   431	    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
   432	       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
   433	       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
   434	       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
   435	       notes: ([
   436	         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
   437	         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
   438	         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),

   440	         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
   441	       ]),
   442	       sprints: $f.sprints,
   443	       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
   444	       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
   445	                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
   446	       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
   447	       written: false}')
   448	
   449	  if (( write )); then
   450	    local why=""
   451	    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
   452	    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
   453	    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
   454	    fi
   455	    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
   456	      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
   457	      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")

   467	    fi
   468	  fi

   470	  if (( json )); then

   473	    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"

   479	cmd_record_round() {
   480	  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
   481	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
   482	  local p th ts now out trip
   483	  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
   484	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
   485	    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
   486	    return 0
   487	  fi
   488	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
   489	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
   490	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
   491	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
   492	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
   493	  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
   494	  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
   495	      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
   496	    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   497	    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
   498	    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
   499	       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
   500	       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
   501	    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
   502	       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
   503	       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
   504	    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
   505	    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
   506	    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
   507	    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
   508	          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
   509	        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
   510	          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
   511	        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
   512	          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
   513	        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
   514	          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
   515	        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
   516	        else null end ) as $trip
   517	    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
   518	    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
   519	      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
   520	      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
   521	      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
   522	    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
   523	  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
   524	  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
   525	  echo "$out"
   526	  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
   527	    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
   528	    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
   529	    return 10
   530	  fi
   531	  return 0
   532	}
   533	
   534	cmd_mark() {
   535	  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
   536	  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
   537	  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
   538	    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
   539	  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
   540	    local err drc=0
   541	    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
   542	    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
   543	  fi
   544	  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
   545	}
   546	
   547	case "$sub" in
   548	  write)  cmd_write ;;
   549	  read)   cmd_read ;;
   550	  derive) cmd_derive ;;
   551	  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
   552	  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
   553	  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   554	  *) usage ;;
   555	esac

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# implement-gate.sh — Dual-mode compliance hook for App Zone writes (FR-7)
4	# =============================================================================
5	# Checks whether Write/Edit to App Zone files occurs within an active
6	# /implement or /bug skill invocation.
7	#
8	# Modes (cycle-129 D-4.1, DEC-0163; .loa.config.yaml implement_gate.mode):
9	#   ask (default; unset or any other value): an unsanctioned App-Zone write asks,
10	#       exactly as before, and now logs one row (decision "ask").
11	#   telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one row (action "telemetry",
12	#       decision "outside_run") and is allowed silently.
13	#   deny: an unsanctioned App-Zone write is DENIED when the run position is
14	#       known: .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and its derived_at is within
15	#       run_mode.stale_hours (12). The gate is a fence only in this mode. An
16	#       unknown position (cache missing, not derived, stale or unparseable)
17	#       falls back to ask (decision "unknown_position"), never to allow.
18	# Sanction (any mode; first match wins; one row each, action "allow"):
19	#   sanctioned_run    — the heuristic below: a fresh RUNNING cache, and its
20	#                       derived_at (when present) within run_mode.stale_hours
21	#   sanctioned_marker — .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint,
22	#                       started_at} with started_at within two hours (written by
23	#                       `run-checkpoint.sh mark`, removed by `unmark`); a stale or
24	#                       malformed marker logs decision "stale_marker" and does not sanction
25	#   override          — LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the hook's environment
26	# Rows go to .run/audit.jsonl as {ts, hook: "implement-gate", action, decision,
27	# mode, path} with path control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes; LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
28	# adds replay: true to every row this gate writes (DEC-0167).
29	#
30	# Claims modifier (implement_gate.claims: authoritative; the legacy
31	# implement_gate.mode: authoritative means mode ask + claims authoritative):
32	#   reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin. The PreToolUse
33	#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
34	#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this modifier.
35	#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
36	#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
37	#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
38	#      non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny with a known position and no
39	#      sanction, is denied) and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
40	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
41	#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask"/"deny" for a non-implementation
42	#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
43	#
44	# `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode [CONFIG]` prints the effective mode (and the
45	# claims modifier) without reading stdin — the /loa Gate line.
46	#
47	# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
48	# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
49	# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
50	#
51	# Failure mode: FAIL-ASK for App Zone writes (not fail-open). A payload jq cannot
52	# parse (or no jq), or a file_path that cannot be canonicalised, asks too (run-2
53	# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
54	# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
55	# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
56	# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
57	# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location
58	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
59	# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
60	# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
61	# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl,
62	# .run/implement-active.json or .loa.config.yaml asks in every mode and under
63	# every sanction, and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
64	# Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.
65	#
66	# Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent
67	# exit 0 with empty stdout; ask = exit 0 with
68	#   {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}
69	# deny = the same shape with "permissionDecision":"deny".
70	# A top-level "decision" accepts approve|block only, so "ask" never goes there.
71	# file_path and active_skill reach stderr only through strip_controls (n21;
72	# run-2 findings 3/12; run-3 finding 5): cut to 256 bytes without splitting a
73	# character, then C0 and DEL, UTF-8 C1 controls and the Unicode format/bidi/tag
74	# code points are removed to a fixed point. Audit rows record the RAW values cut
75	# the same way and written with jq -a, so every non-ASCII code point is \uXXXX:
76	# faithful (implement+U+200B logs as implement\u200b) and terminal-safe (run-3 finding 4).
77	#
78	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — hook must never crash-block.
79	# Parse/read errors on App Zone writes → ask (not allow).
80	#
81	# Part of cycle-049/050: Upstream Platform Alignment (FR-7)
82	# Red Team findings addressed: ATK-005 (state tampering), ATK-006 (fail-open),
83	#   ATK-007 (prompt injection via file path)
84	# Sprint-108 T4.4: Dual-mode (authoritative + heuristic)
85	# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization
86	# =============================================================================
87	
88	# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
89	input=""
90	if [[ "${1:-}" != "--effective-mode" ]]; then
91	    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
92	fi
93	
94	# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
95	# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
96	emit_ask() {
97	    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
98	        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
99	    else
100	        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
101	    fi
102	}
103	
104	# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
105	# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
106	# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
107	# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
108	# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
109	_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
110	_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
111	    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
112	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
113	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
114	    done
115	    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
116	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
117	    done
118	    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
119	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
120	    done

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
   118	    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
   119	    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
   120	    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
   122	    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
   123	    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
   124	    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
   125	    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
   126	    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
   127	    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
   128	    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
   129	     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
   130	     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
   131	    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
   132	    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
   133	        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
   134	        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
   135	        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
   136	        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
   137	        else . end)) as $knobs |
   138	    {
   139	      schema_version: 1,
   140	      id: $id,
   141	      profile: $sel.name,
   142	      profile_source: $sel.source,
   143	      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
   144	      profile_keys: $keys,
   145	      knobs: $knobs,
   146	      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
   147	                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
   148	                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
   149	      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
   150	                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
   151	    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
   152	  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
   153	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
   154	    return 1
   155	  fi
   156	  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
   157	  local w
   158	  while IFS= read -r w; do
   159	    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
   160	  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
   161	  return 0
   162	}
   163	
   164	_loa_pl_write_cache() {
   165	  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
   166	  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
   167	  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
   168	  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
   169	    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
   170	  fi
   171	  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
   172	  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   173	    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   174	  else
   175	    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   176	  fi
   177	  return 0
   178	}
   179	
   180	# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
   181	# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
   182	_loa_pl_load() {
   183	  _loa_pl_paths
   184	  _loa_pl_id
   185	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
   186	    return 0
   187	  fi
   188	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
   189	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
   190	    local j
   191	    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
   192	        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
   193	    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
   194	      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
   195	      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   196	      return 0
   197	    fi
   198	  fi
   199	  _loa_pl_build || return 1
   200	  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   201	  _loa_pl_write_cache
   202	  return 0
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
   206	_loa_pl_live() {
   207	  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
   208	  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   209	    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
   210	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   211	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   212	      return 0
   213	    fi
   214	  fi
   215	  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   216	  return 0
