455	# Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?
456	# Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json, .run/simstim-state.json, .run/state.json
457	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
458	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
459	# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
460	_ig_fresh() {
461	    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
462	    local now last_epoch
463	    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
464	    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
465	        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
466	    else
467	        last_epoch=$(date -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -jf '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
468	    fi
469	    [[ "$last_epoch" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
470	    (( last_epoch > 0 && now - last_epoch <= 86400 && last_epoch - now <= 86400 ))
471	}
472	
473	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $2 parses, is at most $1 seconds old and at most 300 s ahead (clock skew);
474	# jq's fromdateiso8601 keeps it portable (no GNU date -d). Fractional seconds are dropped first
475	_ig_within() {
476	    [[ -n "$2" && "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
477	    jq -en --arg t "$2" --argjson w "$1" \
478	        '($t | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $e | $e != null and (now - $e) <= $w and ($e - now) <= 300' \
479	        >/dev/null 2>&1
480	}
481	
482	# derived_at, when a cache carries one, must be within run_mode.stale_hours (cycle-129 D-4.1)
483	_ig_derived_ok() {
484	    local da
485	    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$1" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
486	    [[ -z "$da" ]] && return 0
487	    _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"
488	}
489	
490	check_implementation_active() {
491	    # Check sprint-plan state
492	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
493	        local state plan_id last_activity
494	        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
495	        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true
496	
497	        # Integrity: must have plan_id
498	        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
499	            return 1
500	        fi
501	
502	        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
503	        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
504	        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
505	        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
506	            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
507	        fi
508	
509	        # A derived cache older than run_mode.stale_hours is not a run position (cycle-129 D-4.1)
510	        if ! _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json"; then
511	            return 1
512	        fi
513	
514	        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
515	            return 0
516	        fi
517	    fi
518	
519	    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
520	    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
521	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
522	        local phase simstim_activity
523	        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
524	        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
525	        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
526	            return 0
527	        fi
528	    fi
529	
530	    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
531	    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
532	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
533	        local run_state run_activity
534	        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
535	        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
536	        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity" && _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/state.json"; then
537	            return 0
538	        fi
539	    fi
540	
541	    return 1
542	}
543	
544	# The implementing skills' marker (run-checkpoint.sh mark): 0 fresh and well-formed, 1 absent, 2 stale or malformed
545	check_implement_marker() {
546	    local f="$RUN_DIR/implement-active.json" started
547	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 1
548	    jq -e '(.skill == "implement" or .skill == "bug") and (.sprint | type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$"))' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
549	    started=$(jq -r '.started_at // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || started=""
550	    _ig_within 7200 "$started" || return 2
551	    return 0
552	}
553	
554	# The derived run position for deny: known only when .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and carries a derived_at
555	# within run_mode.stale_hours; sets position_state (display copy) or position_why
556	position_state=""
557	position_why=""
558	read_position() {
559	    local f="$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" da st
560	    if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then position_why="cache missing"; return 1; fi
561	    if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then position_why="cache unparseable"; return 1; fi
562	    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
563	    if [[ -z "$da" ]]; then position_why="cache not derived"; return 1; fi
564	    if ! _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"; then position_why="cache older than run_mode.stale_hours"; return 1; fi
565	    st=$(jq -r '.state // .status // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || st=""
566	    position_state=$(strip_controls "${st:-unknown}")
567	    [[ -n "$position_state" ]] || position_state="unknown"
568	    return 0
569	}
570	
571	emit_deny() {
572	    jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
573	}
574	deny_reason() {
575	    printf 'App Zone write with no active implementation run (derived position: %s); run /implement or /bug, or set implement_gate.mode: ask' "$position_state"
576	}
577	
578	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
579	# Sanction: a fresh RUNNING cache, a fresh implementing-skill marker, or the
580	# operator's override, in that order — one row for the path that sanctioned
581	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
582	sanction=""
583	if check_implementation_active; then
584	    sanction="sanctioned_run"
585	else
586	    check_implement_marker
587	    marker_rc=$?
588	    if (( marker_rc == 0 )); then
589	        sanction="sanctioned_marker"
590	    elif [[ "${LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
591	        sanction="override"
592	    fi
593	    (( marker_rc == 2 )) && log_gate_row note stale_marker
594	fi
595	
596	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
597	# A non-implementation claim asks whatever the sanction; under deny with a
598	# known position and no sanction it is denied (tighten-only: never looser)
599	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
600	if (( claim_ask )); then
601	    if [[ "$gate_mode" == "deny" && -z "$sanction" ]] && read_position; then
602	        echo "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' denied during /$safe_skill (not an implementation skill; derived position: $position_state)." >&2
603	        log_model_signal deny
604	        emit_deny "$(deny_reason)"
605	        exit 0
606	    fi
607	    echo "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected during /$safe_skill (not an implementation skill)." >&2
608	    log_model_signal ask
609	    emit_ask "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write outside implementation skill. Verify this is intentional."
610	    exit 0
611	fi
612	
613	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
614	# Decision
615	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
616	if [[ -n "$sanction" ]]; then
617	    # Implementation is active (or the operator overrode) — allow the write, one row
618	    log_gate_row allow "$sanction"
619	    exit 0
620	fi
621	
622	case "$gate_mode" in
623	    telemetry)
624	        # Log and allow, silently
625	        log_gate_row telemetry outside_run
626	        exit 0
627	        ;;
628	    deny)
629	        if read_position; then
630	            echo "[GATE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' denied: no active implementation run (derived position: $position_state)." >&2
631	            log_gate_row deny deny
632	            emit_deny "$(deny_reason)"
633	            exit 0
634	        fi
635	        # Unknown position: ask, never allow
636	        echo "[GATE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' outside an active run; run position unknown ($position_why), asking instead of denying." >&2
637	        log_gate_row ask unknown_position
638	        emit_ask "[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation; run position unknown ($position_why). Verify this is intentional."
639	        exit 0
640	        ;;
641	    *)
642	        # No active implementation detected — ADVISORY ask (unchanged), now counted
643	        echo "[ADVISORY] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected outside active /implement or /bug." >&2
644	        echo "No RUNNING state found in .run/ state files. This may bypass review gates." >&2
645	        log_gate_row ask ask
646	        echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation. Verify this is intentional."}}'
647	        exit 0
648	        ;;
649	esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
121:now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }
122-
123-# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
124-# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
125-cfg() {
     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
       notes: ([
         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
       ]),
       sprints: $f.sprints,
       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
       written: false}')

  if (( write )); then
    local why=""
    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
    fi
    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
    else
      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
    fi
  fi

  if (( json )); then
    jq . <<<"$report"
  else
    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_record_round() {
  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  local p th ts now out trip
  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
    return 0
  fi
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
        else null end ) as $trip
    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
  echo "$out"
  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
    return 10
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_mark() {
  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    local err drc=0
    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  fi
  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
}

case "$sub" in
  write)  cmd_write ;;
  read)   cmd_read ;;
  derive) cmd_derive ;;
  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;

+# mode {unset, ask, telemetry, deny} × claims {plain, authoritative} × write {app, trust}
+# × sanction {none, run_fresh, run_stale, marker_fresh, marker_stale, override}

+# $1 cache: fresh | stale | missing | unparseable | run_fresh | run_stale (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache_state() {

+        missing) ;;
+        unparseable) printf '{"state": "RUNNING", \n' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;

+# allow | ask | deny | invalid:<stdout>

+# The expected "<decision> <row>" for one cell; row = action/decision of the write's decision row

+    local mode="$1" claims="$2" wclass="$3" sanction="$4" cache="$5" sanctioned=0 known=0

+        if [[ "$mode" == deny ]] && (( ! sanctioned && known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/ask"; fi
+        return
+    fi
+    if (( sanctioned )); then
+        case "$sanction" in run_fresh) echo "allow allow/sanctioned_run" ;; marker_fresh) echo "allow allow/sanctioned_marker" ;; *) echo "allow allow/override" ;; esac
+        return
+    fi
+    case "$mode" in
+        ask) echo "ask ask/ask" ;;
+        telemetry) echo "allow telemetry/outside_run" ;;
+        deny) if (( known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/unknown_position"; fi ;;

# =============================================================================
# implement-gate.bats — cycle-126 Sprint 4 Task 4.4 (SDD D-4.4, Flatline SKP-008)
#
# The PreToolUse stdin carries no harness-set skill signal
# (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks lists session_id, transcript_path,
# cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id,
# and agent_id/agent_type inside a subagent). tool_input is model-authored,

#   - detect-platform-features.sh never reports the flag true on its own
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0   # `run -1 grep`: a bare `! grep` cannot fail, and only "no match" (exit 1) passes — a missing file (exit 2) fails (sprint-250 review run 2, #10)
    REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    GATE="$REPO/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh"
    DETECT="$REPO/.claude/scripts/detect-platform-features.sh"
    FIX="$REPO/tests/fixtures/pretooluse-payloads"
    ROOT="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
    mkdir -p "$ROOT/.run"
    unset LOA_TEAM_MEMBER CLAUDE_ACTIVE_SKILL_AVAILABLE
}

payload() { sed "s#__ROOT__#$ROOT#g" "$FIX/$1"; }

gate_with() {
    local fixture="$1"
    payload "$fixture" > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
    run --separate-stderr bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
}

# Claude Code PreToolUse contract: "ask" is only valid as hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; a top-level
# "decision" takes approve|block only (sprint-250 audit n20). Allow = silent exit 0 with empty stdout.
decision() {
    if [[ -z "$output" ]]; then echo allow
    elif jq -e '(has("decision") | not) and .hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName == "PreToolUse"
                and .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision == "ask"
                and (.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason | type == "string" and length > 0)' <<<"$output" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ask
    else echo "invalid:$output"; fi
}

opt_in() { printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"; }

    printf '{"active_skill_available":true}\n' > "$ROOT/.run/platform-features.json"
    gate_with write-src-active-implement.json
    [ "$(jq -r '.active_skill_available' "$ROOT/.run/platform-features.json")" = false ]
}

     7	# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
     8	# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
     9	# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
    10	# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
    11	# =============================================================================

    13	setup() {
    14	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"

    28	# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
    29	ledger() {
    30	  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
    31	    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
    32	     cycles: [
    33	       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    34	        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
    35	       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    36	        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    37	                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    38	                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
    39	                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    40	}
    41	
    42	# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
    43	feedback() {
    44	  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
    45	  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"

    47	  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
    48	  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
    49	    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    50	  else
    51	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'

    54	    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
    55	}

    57	# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
     5	# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
     6	# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
     7	# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
     8	# All files live in a temp dir.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    13	  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
    14	  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
    16	  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
    17	  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
    18	  S="$T/.run/state.json"
    19	  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
    20	}
    21	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    22	
    23	# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
    24	fb() {
    25	  local prose
    26	  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
    27	    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    28	  else
    29	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
    30	  fi
    31	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
    32	    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
    33	}
    34	
    35	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

    37	breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
    38	  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
    39	          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
    40	                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
    41	          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
    42	}

    50	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

    53	  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
    54	  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"

    63	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"

+SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
+
+task_raw=""
+if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
+    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
+        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
+                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
+        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
+fi
+KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
+[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
+[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
+
+# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
+if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
+    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
+    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
+        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
+                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
+    fi
+fi
+
+# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
+[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
+[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
+TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
+[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
+
+PRIOR=0
+if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
+    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
+    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
+    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
+fi
+RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
+
+printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
+    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON"

1	# run-mode `/run-halt` and `/run-resume`
     2	
     3	## run-halt
     4	
     5	### Pre-flight
     6	
     7	1. If `.run/state.json` doesn't exist: "ERROR: No run in progress. Nothing to halt." → exit.
     8	2. Read `.state`. If `JACKED_OUT`: "ERROR: Run already completed" → exit. If `HALTED`: "Run is
     9	   already halted. Use `/run-resume` to continue or clean up with `rm -rf .run/`" → exit 0.
    10	
    11	### Execution
    12	
    13	1. Read `run_id`, `target`, `branch`, `phase` from `.run/state.json`; report them plus the halt
    14	   reason (default `"Manual halt"`, or the `--reason` value).
    15	2. If `--force`: warn "current phase interrupted" and skip step 3's phase-completion wait.
    16	3. Otherwise, note phase-completion status per the current `phase`: `IMPLEMENT` → "Implementation
    17	   phase safe to halt" (already committed in cycles); `REVIEW` → "Review can be resumed"; `AUDIT`
    18	   → "Audit can be resumed".
    19	4. Commit pending changes: if `git diff --quiet && git diff --staged --quiet` (nothing pending),
    20	   report "No pending changes to commit" and skip. Otherwise `git add -A` then commit with:
    21	   ```
    22	   WIP: Run halted - {reason}
    23	
    24	   This commit contains work-in-progress from an interrupted Run Mode session.
    25	   Use /run-resume to continue from this point.
    26	
    27	   Run ID: {run_id}
    28	   Target: {target}
    29	   Cycle: {cycles.current}
    30	   Phase: {phase}
    31	   ```
    32	5. Push: `.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh push origin "$branch"`.
    33	6. Create or update the incomplete PR. Check for an existing PR first:
    34	   `gh pr list --head "$branch" --json number -q '.[0].number'`. If found, `gh pr edit $number
    35	   --title "[INCOMPLETE] Run Mode: $target" --body "$body"`; else
    36	   `.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh pr-create "[INCOMPLETE] Run Mode: $target" "$body" --draft`.
    37	   PR body template:
    38	   → verbatim block: `resources/render-templates.md` §halt-incomplete-pr-body
    39	7. Update state atomically (`.state` is canonical): `jq --arg r "$reason" --arg ts "$timestamp" '.state = "HALTED" | .halt = {"reason": $r, "timestamp": $ts} | .timestamps.last_activity = $ts'`.
    40	8. Report the halt summary box:
    41	   → verbatim block: `resources/render-templates.md` §halt-summary-box
    42	
    43	## run-resume
    44	
    45	### Pre-flight

# FR-SZ — State-Zone executable/lifecycle write guard (sprint-bug-213 / #1044)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Blocks DIRECT inline agent writes to the executable / lifecycle-controlled
# subset of the State Zone, which the shipped Bash allow-list (cp/tee/cat/echo/
# python3/bash/sh/ln/dd/tar/sed/...) otherwise permits with no prompt:
#   - .run/cron.d           deferred-execution cron scripts (dir + descendants)
#   - .run/...*.sh          sourced for model routing (incl. merged-model-aliases.sh)
#   - grimoires/loa/skills  skill-approval lifecycle (dir + descendants)
# Companion tool-layer half: the Write/Edit deny rules in .claude/settings.json
# (deny > allow). A Write-only deny without this Bash guard is theater (#1044).
#
# SCOPE (validated): the PreToolUse:Bash hook sees only the agent's OUTER command
# string. A generator invoked as `python3 .../model-overlay-hook.py` or `bash X.sh`
# that writes these paths INTERNALLY is invisible here (the redirect lives inside an
# already-approved subprocess) — so this guard blocks only DIRECT inline writes and
# leaves the legitimate generators frictionless (recon: zero inline callers).
#
# Coverage (sprint-bug-213 iter-2, cross-model dissent CR-1..CR-5): directory
# destinations with or without a trailing slash; option-form destinations
# (-t/--target-directory for the copy family, -C/--directory for tar, -d for unzip);
# tee long-options and non-first operands; grouped/long in-place editor flags
# (-Ei, --in-place); and a trailing shell comment as a statement terminator.
#
# Accepted bypass classes (defense-in-depth fence, NOT a hardened boundary; cf. the
# header section-11 list): post-cd relative writes, variable-indirected targets,
# obfuscated interpreter writes (base64/concat path in -c), a pipe-delimited sed
# in-place edit (the statement-bound stops at the first pipe), git checkout of a
# tracked path, non-allow-listed writers (truncate/sponge/ex/ed already prompt),
# and a trailing comment that merely mentions a protected path. Sanctioned override
# for the skill-audit approve move + operator use: LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE=1.
#
# pass-2: only the cheap OUTER gate below was converted to _match (it runs on
# every Bash call). The inner write-intent greps fire only when the command
# already mentions a protected path — left as grep because their `\btee\b…`,
# `\bdd\b…[^|;&]*` shapes do not admit a provably-isomorphic consuming \b
# translation (the boundary char can be the first char of the next element).
# pass-8 pre-filter: the outer-gate ERE is a three-branch alternation whose
# branches mandate, respectively, the literals `.run/` (from \.run/…\.sh),
# `.run/cron.d` (⊃ `.run/`), and `grimoires/loa/skills`. The guard tests the
# two distinct covering literals — either present ⇒ evaluate the gate.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Path fragments (ERE; substring match also covers absolute / $PWD-prefixed forms).
_sz_pc="[^[:space:]'\";&|#]"                              # one path character
_sz_sh="\\.run/${_sz_pc}*\\.sh"                          # a .sh file anywhere under .run/
_sz_root="(\\.run/cron\\.d|grimoires/loa/skills)"        # protected directory roots
_sz_tgt="(${_sz_sh}|${_sz_root}(/${_sz_pc}*)?)"          # a protected target (file OR dir[/desc])
_sz_file="(${_sz_sh}|${_sz_root}/${_sz_pc}*)"            # a protected descendant FILE
_sz_b="([[:space:]]|['\"]|[;&|#]|\$)"                    # right token boundary (NOT '/')
_sz_end="([[:space:]]+--?[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*)*[[:space:]]*([;&|#]|\$)"  # end-of-stmt; allows trailing option flags (GNU options-after-operands)
_sz_pre="${_sz_pc}*"                                     # optional leading path prefix (./, abs, $PWD/, repo-root)

if [[ "$command" == *".run/"* || "$command" == *"grimoires/loa/skills"* ]] \
   && _match "(${_sz_sh}|\\.run/cron\\.d|grimoires/loa/skills)"; then
  if [[ "${LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    # Sanctioned override — allow, warn once, audit the bypass (best-effort).
    if [[ -z "${LOA_SZ_EXEC_WRITE_BYPASS_WARNED:-}" ]]; then
      echo "WARNING: block-destructive-bash: LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE=1 — State-Zone executable/lifecycle write guard bypassed this session." >&2
      export LOA_SZ_EXEC_WRITE_BYPASS_WARNED=1
    fi
    {
      _sz_redactor="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.claude/scripts/lib/log-redactor.sh"
      _sz_cmd=$(printf '%s' "$command" | "$_sz_redactor" 2>/dev/null) || _sz_cmd="[REDACTOR-FAILED]"
      [[ ${#_sz_cmd} -gt 2048 ]] && _sz_cmd="${_sz_cmd:0:2048}[...TRUNCATED]"
      mkdir -p "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run" 2>/dev/null || true
      TZ=UTC0 printf -v _sz_ts '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
      # @guard fence:FR-SZ
      jq -cn --arg ts "$_sz_ts" --arg cmd "$_sz_cmd" --arg cwd "$PWD" --arg replay "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" \
        '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $cmd, exit_code: 0, cwd: $cwd, hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "bypass", pattern_id: "FR-SZ"} + (if $replay == "1" then {replay: true} else {} end)' \
        >> "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
    } 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # Write-intent tests — first match blocks (emit_block exits 2). Anchored to write
    # operations so read-only references (cat/ls/grep/source/cp-FROM) pass through.

    # SZ-REDIR: redirect (any fd / append / noclobber-override) INTO a protected file.
    if echo "$_cmd_match" | grep -qE "([0-9]*|&)?>>?\\|?[[:space:]]*['\"]?${_sz_pre}${_sz_file}${_sz_b}" 2>/dev/null; then
      matched=$(echo "$_cmd_match" | grep -oE ">>?[[:space:]]*['\"]?${_sz_pre}${_sz_file}" | head -1)
      # @guard fence:FR-SZ-REDIR
# FR-SZ2 — System-Zone (.claude/) direct Bash writes (cycle-122)
# Closes the single-agent gap: zone-write-guard fences Write/Edit tools, the
# team guards fence teammates, but a plain-shell `echo x > .claude/foo` or
# `sed -i` on a hook passed every wired fence. Same trust posture as
# zone-write-guard: the bounded framework-dev marker
# (.run/zone-guard-authorization.json — scope=framework, RFC3339 expires_at,
# 24h mtime cap; test override via LOA_ZONE_GUARD_AUTH_FILE) authorizes
# upstream self-development sessions, audited per-session. Sanctioned paths
# `.claude/overrides/` and `.claude/cache/` are excluded (they are the
# documented customization/runtime surfaces). LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE=1
# is honored with the same warn+audit semantics as FR-SZ.
# Shapes: redirect, tee, copy-family dest, sed-in-place, rm. Same accepted
# bypass classes as FR-SZ (fence, not boundary).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *".."* ]]; then
  # traversal-looking command: no exclusions (a path like
  # .claude/overrides/../hooks/x resolves back into protected space)
  _c2_cmd="$_cmd_match"
else
  _c2_cmd="${_cmd_match//.claude\/overrides/.EXCLUDED-OVR}"
  _c2_cmd="${_c2_cmd//.claude\/cache/.EXCLUDED-CACHE}"
fi
if [[ "$_c2_cmd" == *".claude/"* ]]; then
  _c2_file="\\.claude/${_sz_pc}+"
  _c2_tgt="\\.claude(/${_sz_pc}*)?"
  _c2_authorized=""
  # 1) env override (operator terminals) — same var as FR-SZ
  if [[ "${LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    _c2_authorized="env"
  else
    # 2) bounded framework-dev marker (mirrors zone-write-guard validation)
    _c2_auth_file="${LOA_ZONE_GUARD_AUTH_FILE:-${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run/zone-guard-authorization.json}"
    if [[ -f "$_c2_auth_file" ]] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      _c2_row="$(jq -r 'select(type=="object" and .scope=="framework"
                          and (.reason|type=="string") and ((.reason|length)>0)
                          and (.expires_at|type=="string")
                          and (.expires_at|test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$")))
                        | .expires_at' "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null)" || _c2_row=""
      if [[ -n "$_c2_row" ]]; then
        TZ=UTC0 printf -v _c2_now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
        printf -v _c2_epoch '%(%s)T' -1
        _c2_mtime="$(stat -Lc '%Y' -- "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null || stat -Lf '%m' -- "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        if [[ "$_c2_mtime" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( _c2_epoch - _c2_mtime <= 86400 )) && [[ "$_c2_now" < "$_c2_row" ]]; then
          _c2_authorized="marker"
        fi
      fi
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -z "$_c2_authorized" ]]; then
    if echo "$_c2_cmd" | grep -qE "([0-9]*|&)?>>?\\|?[[:space:]]*['\"]?${_sz_pre}${_c2_file}${_sz_b}" 2>/dev/null; then
      matched=$(echo "$_c2_cmd" | grep -oE ">>?[[:space:]]*['\"]?${_sz_pre}${_c2_file}" | head -1)
      # @guard fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
      emit_block "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$matched" "Direct shell write into .claude/ (System Zone — framework-managed). Use .claude/overrides/ or .loa.config.yaml for customization; upstream framework dev uses the bounded marker (.run/zone-guard-authorization.json) or LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE=1 (audited)."
    fi
    if echo "$_c2_cmd" | grep -qE "\\btee\\b[^|;&]*[[:space:]]['\"]?${_sz_pre}${_c2_file}${_sz_b}" 2>/dev/null; then
      matched=$(echo "$_c2_cmd" | grep -oE "${_c2_file}" | head -1)
      # @guard fence:FR-SZ2-TEE

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-decisions-surface.sh: SessionStart hook that surfaces pending decision rows.
#
# Prints up to 10 `proposed` then `open` rows of grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (id, status,
# summary only) so the operator sees what awaits /decisions confirm. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on
# `decisions.surface_at_session_start` (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
#
# CONTRACT (observability, never a gate; same as loa-kf-surface.sh):
#   - Exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session.
#   - Disabled or no config: prints nothing (read with yq, or a plain-text fallback without it).
#   - Enabled but Mike Farah yq v4 or jq is missing, or the ledger is unreadable or has an
#     unknown schema_version: one "[DECISIONS] WARNING ..." line on stdout.
#   - Enabled and healthy: the block on stdout (SessionStart injects stdout as context);
#     nothing when no row is open or proposed and no marker is stale.
#   - A stale .run/unattended.json (another session, or older than
#     decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours, default 24) adds one notice line.
#
# TRUST BOUNDARY: row text is agent-authored and UNTRUSTED. Only id, status and summary are
#   read; each summary is control-stripped (C0, C1, U+2028/9), angle brackets are replaced so
#   no tag can close the fence, and it is capped at 100 characters. The whole block is then
#   wrapped by the L6 data fence, sanitize_for_session_start L6 <block> --max-chars 2000
#   (context-isolation-lib.sh). Without that sanitizer the block is not printed.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"

# Test seam (mirrors loa-kf-surface.sh): overrides are honoured only under
# LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats marker present.
_dec_test_mode_active() {
  [[ "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" || -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]
}

have_yq4=0
if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]]; then have_yq4=1; fi

# The config is read first (yq, or a plain-text fallback without it), so an enabled surface on a host
# without its tools says so instead of looking disabled.
config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
enabled="false"
if _dec_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
  enabled="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
elif [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
  if [[ $have_yq4 -eq 1 ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
      enabled="$(loa_knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
  else
    # top-level `decisions:` block, then an indented `surface_at_session_start: true`
    enabled="$(awk '
      /^[^[:space:]#]/ { blk = ($0 ~ /^decisions:[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/) }
      blk && /^[[:space:]]+surface_at_session_start:[[:space:]]*true[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/ { print "true"; exit }
    ' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi
fi
[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0

missing=""
[[ $have_yq4 -eq 1 ]] || missing="Mike Farah yq v4"
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="${missing:+${missing} and }jq"
if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: the decisions surface is enabled but ${missing} is missing; rows are not shown. Install it, or set decisions.surface_at_session_start: false."
  exit 0
fi

LEDGER="${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
RUN_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/.run"
if _dec_test_mode_active; then
  [[ -n "${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE:-}" ]] && LEDGER="${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE}"
  [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR:-}" ]] && RUN_DIR="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR}"
fi

+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading

+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"

+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }

+    case "$rc" in

+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac

+  fi

+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
+# is not optional.
+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$o_heading"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local tmp="${file}.prune-tmp" rc=0
+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
+    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }
+    state == "" && $0 == heading { state = "head"; n = 0; buf[++n] = $0; next }
+    state == "head" {
+      if (index($0, start)) { state = "skip"; n = 0; next }
+      if ($0 ~ /^\|/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) { buf[++n] = $0; next }
+      flush(); state = ""; print; next
+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in
+      3) log "ERROR: ${file}: no end marker for optional section '${section}'" ;;
+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  verbose "Pruned empty optional section ${section} (${heading}) from ${file}"
+}

name: Prompt Budget

# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1): the always-loaded prompt surface has hard byte
# budgets — SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read resources),
# CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn > 114,688 B).
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh is the gate; the two sentinel steps prove the
# gate itself still bites (a scanner that exits 0 from a syntax error must not
# read as green).

on:
  # Every pull request: the gate takes seconds, and a path filter would miss the
  # shared inputs the checker charges (skill includes rendered into SKILL.md,
  # resources read unconditionally, the keep list) — Bridgebuilder F-001 on
  # PR #1266.
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  prompt-budget:
    name: Byte budgets for the prompt surface
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5

      - name: Check budgets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json > prompt-budget.json || rc=$?
          # A checker that dies before writing a report must fail LOUD with its
          # exit code, not as an opaque jq parse error (Bridgebuilder F-003).
          if ! jq -e . prompt-budget.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh --json produced no parseable report (exit $rc)"
            cat prompt-budget.json || true
            exit 1
          fi
          # Human-readable table for the log; the JSON gate below is the verdict.
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh || echo "::notice::human-readable run exited non-zero; the JSON gate decides"
          jq -r '.violations[]? | "::error::prompt budget: \(.)"' prompt-budget.json
          jq -e '.ok' prompt-budget.json >/dev/null

      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the over-budget sentinel with exit 1)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over --quiet || rc=$?
          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh did not reject tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over with exit 1 (got $rc)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: over-budget sentinel rejected"

      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the under-budget sentinel)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |

# ============================================================================
# Bootstrap: insert markers into target files
# ============================================================================

# Anchor patterns: section_name|start_regex|end_regex
readonly -a ANCHORS=(
  "process_compliance_never|^### NEVER Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "process_compliance_always|^### ALWAYS Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|^### Task Tracking Hierarchy$|^$|^---$"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|^## Pre-Implementation Checklist$|^## |^---$"
  "autonomous_agent_constraints|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_ANCHOR|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_END"
  "simstim_constraints|SIMSTIM_SKILL_ANCHOR|SIMSTIM_SKILL_END"
  "implementing_tasks_constraints|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_ANCHOR|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_END"
)

bootstrap_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    verbose "Section ${section} already has markers in ${file}, skipping bootstrap"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find anchor for this section
  local anchor_start="" anchor_end=""
  for anchor in "${ANCHORS[@]}"; do
    local a_section a_start a_end
    IFS='|' read -r a_section a_start a_end <<< "$anchor"
    if [[ "$a_section" == "$section" ]]; then
      anchor_start="$a_start"
      anchor_end="$a_end"
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ -z "$anchor_start" ]]; then
    log "WARNING: No anchor defined for section ${section}, skipping"
    return 0
  fi

  # For skill-md sections, use <constraints> tags
  if [[ "$anchor_start" == *"SKILL_ANCHOR"* ]]; then
    verbose "Skill section ${section}: markers will be inserted inside <constraints> block during generation"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find the anchor line and insert markers after the table header
  local matches
  matches=$(grep -c "$anchor_start" "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [[ "$matches" -ne 1 ]]; then
    log "ERROR: Anchor '${anchor_start}' matches ${matches} times in ${file} (expected 1)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Find the section: locate header, keep table header+separator, wrap data rows with markers
  local tmp="${file}.bootstrap-tmp"
  local end_pat1="${anchor_end%%|*}"
  local end_pat2="${anchor_end#*|}"
  awk -v anchor="$anchor_start" \
      -v end_pat1="$end_pat1" \
      -v end_pat2="$end_pat2" \
      -v start_m="$start_marker" \
      -v warning_m="$warning" \
      -v end_m="$end_marker" \
      -v content_m="$content" \
      '
      BEGIN { state="looking"; sep_seen=0 }
      state == "looking" && $0 ~ anchor {
        print; state="in_header"; next
      }
      state == "in_header" {
        # Print everything until we see the separator row (|---|)
        print
        if ($0 ~ /^\|[-|: ]+\|$/) {
          sep_seen=1
          print start_m
          print warning_m
          printf "%s\n", content_m
          state="skipping"
        }
        next
      }
      state == "skipping" {
        if ($0 ~ end_pat1 || $0 ~ end_pat2) {
          print end_m
          if ($0 !~ /^$/) print
          state="done"
          next
        }
        # Skip original data rows (replaced by generated content)
        next
      }
      state != "skipping" { print }
      END {
        if (state == "skipping") print end_m
      }
      ' "$file" > "$tmp"

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    diff -u "$file" "$tmp" || true
    rm -f "$tmp"
  else
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    log "Bootstrapped markers for section '${section}' in ${file}"
  fi
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
     3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
     4	# DEC-0141).
     5	#
     6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
     7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
     8	# PER TASK:
     9	#
    10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
    11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
    12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
    13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
    14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
    15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
    16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
    17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
    18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
    19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
    20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
    21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
    22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
    23	#
    24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
    25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
    26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
    27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
    28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
    29	#
    30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
    31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
    32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
    33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
    34	# file is not written through.
    35	#
    36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
    37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
    38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
    39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
    40	#
    41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
    42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
    43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
    44	# full each time and those caches are gone.
    45	
    46	set -uo pipefail
    47	umask 077
    48	export LC_ALL=C
    49	
    50	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    51	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
    52	[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
    53	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
    54	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
    55	DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
    56	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
    57	DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
    58	STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
    59	SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
    60	LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
    61	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
    62	CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
    63	KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
    64	[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20
    65	
    66	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    67	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    68	[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0
    69	
    70	# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
    71	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    72	source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    73	if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
    74	switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
    75	case "$switch" in
    76	    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
    77	esac
    78	THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
    79	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
    80	THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))
    81	
    82	# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
    83	payload="$(cat)"
    84	[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
    85	fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    86	    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    87	    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
    88	            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
    89	            else 1 end;
    90	    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    91	    select(type == "object") |
    92	    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    93	    ([($tn | tojson),
    94	      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
    95	       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
    96	       else 0 end | tostring),
    97	      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
    98	      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
    99	      (now | todate)] | .[])
   100	' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
   101	{
   102	    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
   103	    IFS= read -r LINES
   104	    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
   105	    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
   106	    IFS= read -r TS
   107	} <<< "$fields"
   108	case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
   109	    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
   110	    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
   111	    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
   112	    *) exit 0 ;;
   113	esac
   114	[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
   115	[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0
   116	
   117	# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
   118	_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
   119	    local s
   120	    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
   121	    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
   122	    printf '%s' "$s"
   123	}
   124	payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
   125	SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   126	[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
   127	SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
   128	
   129	task_raw=""
   130	if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
   131	    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
   132	        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
   133	                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
   134	        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
   135	fi
   136	KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
   137	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
   138	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
   139	
   140	# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
   141	if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
   142	    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
   143	    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
   144	        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
   145	                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
   146	    fi
   147	fi
   148	
   149	# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
   150	[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
   151	[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   152	TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
   153	[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
   154	
   155	PRIOR=0
   156	if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
   157	    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
   158	    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
   159	    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
   160	fi
   161	RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
   162	
   163	printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
   164	    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   165	
   166	# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
   167	# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
   168	n=0
   169	while IFS= read -r old; do
   170	    n=$((n + 1))
   171	    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
   172	        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
   173	    fi
   174	done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)
   175	
   176	# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
   177	OVER=false
   178	(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
   179	sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
   180	[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
   181	if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
   182	    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
   183	    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
   184	            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   185	        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   186	    else
   187	        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   188	    fi
   189	fi
   190	
   191	# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
   192	if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
   193	    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2
   194	
   195	    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
   196	        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
   197	        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
   198	        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
   199	    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
   200	    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
   201	    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
   202	    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   203	    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
   204	        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
   205	        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   206	fi
   207	
   208	exit 0

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
     4	#
     5	# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
     6	# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
     7	# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
     8	# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
     9	# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
    10	# =============================================================================
    11	
    12	setup() {
    13	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    14	    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
    15	    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
    16	    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
    17	    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
    18	    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
    19	    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    20	    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    21	}
    22	
    23	# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
    24	# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
    25	add_team_block() {
    26	    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
    27	import sys
    28	p = sys.argv[1]
    29	s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
    30	anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
    31	block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
    32	         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
    33	         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
    34	         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
    35	         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
    36	assert s.count(anchor) == 1
    37	open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
    38	PY
    39	}
    40	
    41	add_team_row() {
    42	    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
    43	        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
    44	        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
    45	        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
    46	    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    47	}

    49	gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }
    50	
    51	@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {

    53	        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    54	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    55	    [ "$output" = "0" ]
    56	}
    57	
    58	@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {
    59	    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    60	    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    61	}
    62	
    63	@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {
    64	    add_team_block

    69	    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    70	    # The neighbouring sections survive with one blank line between them.
    71	    grep -qF '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    72	    run grep -c '^## Agent-Network Primitives$' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

    76	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    77	}

    81	    gen

    94	    grep -qxF '| MUST fixture rule | fixture why |' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    95	    ! grep -qF 'MUST stale row' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    96	}
    97

    99	    add_team_row

   101	    run gen
   102	    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
   103	    [[ "$output" == *"Missing markers"*"agent_teams_constraints"* ]]
   104	    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
   105	}
   106

   108	    add_team_block
   109	    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
   110	import sys
   111	p = sys.argv[1]

   113	s = s.replace("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |", "## Agent Teams\n\nOperator prose that is not a table.\n\n| Rule | Why |")
   114	open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
   115	PY
   116	    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
   117	    run gen
   118	    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
   119	    [[ "$output" == *"no '## Agent Teams' heading directly above its table"* ]]
   120	    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
   121	}
   122

   124	    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash '$LINT' --json"
   125	    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.message | test("agent_teams_constraints: table presence matches"))' >/dev/null
