#!/usr/bin/env bash
# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy enforcement v1
# (#961 K-1 / FR-1)
#
# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Reads tool_input JSON from stdin,
# accumulates session diff lines at .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl, and emits
# a `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the running
# total exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100).
#
# Non-blocking by design — returns 0 regardless. The `enforce: block` config
# semantic is RESERVED for v2; v1 honors `warn` only to avoid surprise breakage
# during initial rollout. See grimoires/loa/sdd.md §3.3 + §7 R-3.
#
# Safety invariants (NFR-Sec-1):
#   - tool_input.content / tool_input.new_string NEVER written to state or
#     trajectory. Only line counts + file paths are recorded.
#   - file_path is JSON-escaped inside jq (tojson — the same encoder the old
#     `jq --arg` path used) — no shell-injection vector.
#   - Hook MUST exit 0 even when yq/jq are missing or config is malformed
#     (graceful degradation; never break Write/Edit due to hook env issues).
#
# perf pass-3 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): jq/yq single-pass consolidation.
# Was (warn regime, the production steady state): yq x2 + jq x7 + wc x2 +
# tr x2 + cat + date x3 + awk. Now: yq x1 + jq x1 + awk + mkdir/dirname.
# Design + isomorphism notes:
#   - ONE yq derives two guaranteed-single-line decision tokens: (1) whether
#     the master switch renders as an explicit false-equivalent (the same
#     ten-token list the old bash `case` matched against the $()-stripped
#     rendering — tostring + sub("\n+$";"") reproduces that stripping), and
#     (2) the threshold rendering when it matches ^[0-9]+$, else "DEFAULT"
#     (the old bash regex guard, applied inside yq so multi-line values
#     cannot pollute line-based token reads). A grep-style "config lacks the
#     key" pre-check was REJECTED: YAML double-quoted keys can be spelled
#     with escape sequences, so textual absence does not prove key absence.
#   - ONE jq (slurp) replaces: `jq empty` validation, tool_name extraction,
#     the content/new_string line count (jq|wc -l|tr), file_path extraction,
#     the files_modified jq -rs aggregation and the wc -l tool_call_count.
#     Line counts replicate `jq -r ... | wc -l` byte semantics exactly:
#     strings count split("\n") segments (empty string = 1, matching the
#     old raw-output trailing newline), null/false vanish via `// empty`
#     (0), other scalars are 1 line, and containers use a recursive
#     pretty-print line-count (def jl) that matches jq's pretty renderer
#     (host-verified against wc -l on nested fixtures).
#   - files_modified/tool_call_count are computed analytically PRE-append
#     ([state files] + current file | unique; NL-count + 1) — provably equal
#     to the old POST-append `jq -rs`/`wc -l` reads for every hook-written
#     state file, including the unterminated-final-line case. The jq -rs
#     wholesale-failure semantic (ANY malformed state line -> 0) is
#     replicated with a try/catch around a per-line fromjson parse.
#     (Out-of-contract shapes an external writer could create — multi-line
#     pretty JSON docs or whitespace-only lines — count as malformed here
#     where the old stream parser tolerated them; state is hook-written.)
#   - The state line and trajectory event are printf-assembled from
#     jq-pre-encoded pieces (tojson == the old jq -nc --arg encoder, key
#     order preserved) — byte-identical output, zero builder spawns.
#   - Timestamps: now|todate == date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ (host-verified);
#     the trajectory filename date is the timestamp's date field (single
#     clock read — removes a midnight-straddle inconsistency, same as the
#     pass-2 zone-guard change). The session-id date (LOA_SESSION_ID unset)
#     uses gmtime|strftime("%Y%m%d") — same UTC day.
#   - Field transport is NUL-delimited ("[0] | implode" builds the NUL;
#     no escape literal appears in this file): file paths and tool names
#     can contain tabs/newlines, which @tsv would rewrite. Embedded JSON
#     NUL escapes (backslash-u-0000) are stripped via string division AND
#     trailing newlines are stripped (scap) — byte-identical to the old $()
#     substitution (minus bash's cosmetic "ignored null byte" warning).
#     Non-string tool_name/file_path values (out of hook contract) render
#     via tojson (compact) where the old jq -r pretty-printed containers;
#     scalars are byte-identical and every non-Write/Edit/NotebookEdit
#     rendering exits 0 through the same case fall-through as before.
#   - Error-shape parity: jq parse failure (invalid JSON stdin) exits 0
#     exactly like the old `jq empty || exit 0`; a post-validation
#     extraction error (e.g. non-object top-level doc) surfaces as an
#     in-band __KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__ marker and exits 5, the code the old
#     set -e death propagated from the failing extraction pipeline.
#     Multi-document stdin (not producible by Claude Code) keeps the old
#     concatenated-rendering semantics via slurp+join("\n").
#
# perf pass-4 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): redundant-spawn elimination — the
# remaining dirname x2 + mkdir x2 drop out of the steady state: SCRIPT_DIR
# uses the pass-2 parameter-expansion idiom; the state-dir mkdir is skipped
# when a [[ -d ]] probe proves the parent exists (guard passing ⇒ dirname's
# target exists ⇒ mkdir -p is a no-op; ANY other shape — no slash, trailing
# slash, missing parent — falls back to the old dirname+mkdir command
# unchanged); the warn-path trajectory mkdir gets the same [[ -d ]] guard.
# The running-total awk read was NOT merged into the jq pass (deliberate
# skip): awk's tolerant textual parse counts lines_changed from lines that
# are not valid JSON (e.g. a crash-truncated final line), which the jq
# fromjson path cannot replicate without reimplementing strtod-prefix
# numeric parsing — behavior on truncated state files would diverge.
#
# perf pass-6 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): memoization — the pass-3 two-token
# yq derivation is a PURE function of the config file's bytes, re-derived on
# EVERY Write/Edit. The token array is now cached at
# .run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens (.run/ is State-Zone,
# gitignored). Design notes:
#   - Cache format: line 1 = key "<ns-mtime>:<size>:<abs-path>" of the
#     config (ONE GNU-first `stat -Lc '%y:%s'` spawn — cheaper than the yq
#     it replaces; non-GNU stat ⇒ no key ⇒ never cache, always parse);
#     remaining lines = the _cfg_tokens array joined by newlines. %y is
#     nanosecond mtime (same-second edits rotate the key); the abs-path
#     component keeps two repos/worktrees sharing a relative
#     LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE name from cross-contaminating.
#   - COLD path is the ORIGINAL procsub mapfile verbatim (byte-identical
#     behavior including yq-failure partial output); the cache write is
#     atomic ($$-temp + mv -f -T, same dir; readers see old or new file,
#     never a torn one; concurrent writers: last wins) and any write
#     failure is swallowed. WARM path reconstructs the exact token array;
#     ANY anomaly (missing/corrupt/unreadable cache, key mismatch, stat
#     failure) falls through to the cold path and rewrites the cache. An
#     edit to the config is reflected in the very next invocation (key is
#     stat'd BEFORE the parse — a racing write self-heals next call).
#   - Token round-trip is exact for every yq-emittable stream here: both
#     tokens are guaranteed single-line and non-empty by the yq program
#     (bool literal / digits-or-DEFAULT). TRAILING empty tokens would not
#     survive the $(<cache) trailing-newline strip — unreachable, and even
#     if reached the downstream defaults coincide ("" and unset both yield
#     THRESHOLD=100; "" != "true" for the switch either way). Mid-stream
#     empty tokens round-trip exactly. Cached tokens are NUL-free by
#     construction (bash variables cannot hold NUL).
#   - Trust: config is already attacker-equivalent to the cache — anyone
#     who can write .run/perf-cache/ can write .loa.config.yaml (same
#     operator-writable trust domain), and this hook is non-blocking
#     (warn-only) by design.
#   - If the two-token yq program EVER changes, bump the cache filename
#     version (v1 → v2). jq/yq availability checks stay unconditional so
#     tool-absent behavior is unchanged.
#
# perf pass-7 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): O(n) -> O(delta/1) on the growing
# state file via an incremental aggregate cache at
# .run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg. FULL DESIGN NOTES are at the very
# BOTTOM of this file, AFTER the final `exit 0` — bash never parses past an
# executed exit, so the commentary costs zero runtime on the per-Write/Edit
# hot path (measured ~0.35ms/KB of pre-exit comment lexing on this host).

set -euo pipefail
umask 077

# perf pass-4: was $(cd "$(dirname BASH_SOURCE)" && pwd). ${p%/*} equals
# dirname for every slash-containing script path; the two unreachable-in-
# production shapes (bare filename via PATH-less invocation → ".", root-level
# script "/x.sh" → "/") are covered explicitly. The cd/pwd canonicalization
# subshell is retained. (Idiom copied from the pass-2 zone-write-guard.)
_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
if [[ "${_src_dir}" == "${_src}" ]]; then _src_dir="."; fi
if [[ -z "${_src_dir}" ]]; then _src_dir="/"; fi
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "${_src_dir}" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml}"
TASK_STATE="${KARPATHY_TASK_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"

# Graceful degradation: missing tools or config → no-op.
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# Fast-path: master switch off → no-op (<10ms target).
# NOTE: yq's `// true` defaults trip on explicit `false` values (`false` is
# treated as null by the alternative operator). Read raw, then test for the
# specific false-equivalents (token 1). Token 2 carries the threshold.
# perf pass-6: token array memoized keyed on config identity (header note);
# any cache anomaly falls through to the original yq parse below.
_KP_CACHE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens"
_kp_src="$CONFIG"
[[ "$_kp_src" != /* ]] && _kp_src="$PWD/$_kp_src"
# perf pass-7: ONE stat now serves both the pass-6 config-cache key (%y:%s,
# reassembled byte-identically from the %s/%y fields) and the pass-7
# state-cache identity — the second stat spawn folds into the first. %n
# prefixes each output line so a missing file cannot shift the mapping (GNU
# stat keeps printing the surviving arguments after a failure). Pathological
# '|'-bearing paths can only make a prefix-match miss or collide, leaving
# fields empty/invalid = fail-open (no cache, original behavior).
_kp7_st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%d|%i|%s|%y' -- "$CONFIG" "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) || true
_kp_id=""
_kp7_pre=""
while IFS= read -r _kp7_l; do
    case "$_kp7_l" in
        "$CONFIG|"*)
            IFS='|' read -r _kp7_cd _kp7_ci _kp7_cs _kp7_cy <<< "${_kp7_l#"$CONFIG|"}"
            [[ -n "${_kp7_cy:-}" && -n "${_kp7_cs:-}" ]] && _kp_id="${_kp7_cy}:${_kp7_cs}"
            ;;
        "$TASK_STATE|"*)
            _kp7_pre="${_kp7_l#"$TASK_STATE|"}"
            ;;
    esac
done <<< "$_kp7_st"
_kp_key=""
[[ -n "$_kp_id" ]] && _kp_key="${_kp_id}:${_kp_src}"
_cfg_tokens=()
_kp_hit=0
if [[ -n "$_kp_key" && -f "$_KP_CACHE_FILE" ]]; then
    # Slurp via the read builtin, NOT $(<file): a failed $(<file) redirection
    # aborts an errexit shell even inside a || list (host-probed, bash 5.2)
    # and leaks a bash error line; read -rd '' returns empty on missing/
    # unreadable/dir/NUL-torn inputs — exactly the fail-open we need — and
    # preserves the file bytes verbatim ("<key>\n<tokens...>", the payload
    # carrying no trailing newline by construction of the writer below; an
    # empty payload means a validly-cached EMPTY token stream = yq failure).

input.command: mkdir -p $HOME/bin && cp /tmp/jqbin/jq $HOME/bin/jq && chmod +x $HOME/bin/jq && $HOME/bin/jq --version && $HOME/bin/jq -n --arg label x '$label'; echo $HOME

jq-1.7.1
"x"
/home/evaluser

input.command: cd /workspace/pr; sed -n 200,420p base/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh

content.content:
# empty payload means a validly-cached EMPTY token stream = yq failure).
    _kp_cached=""
    IFS= read -rd '' _kp_cached 2>/dev/null < "$_KP_CACHE_FILE" || true
    if [[ "$_kp_cached" == "$_kp_key"$'\n'* ]]; then
        _kp_payload="${_kp_cached#*$'\n'}"
        [[ -n "$_kp_payload" ]] && mapfile -t _cfg_tokens <<< "$_kp_payload"
        _kp_hit=1
    fi
fi
if [[ "$_kp_hit" -eq 0 ]]; then
    mapfile -t _cfg_tokens < <(
        yq -r '(.karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning | tostring | sub("\n+$"; "") | (. == "false" or . == "False" or . == "FALSE" or . == "0" or . == "no" or . == "No" or . == "NO" or . == "off" or . == "Off" or . == "OFF")),
               (.karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task | tostring | sub("\n+$"; "") | (with(select(test("^[0-9]+$") | not); . = "DEFAULT")))' \
            "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null
    )
    if [[ -n "$_kp_key" ]]; then
        _kp_payload=""
        if [[ "${#_cfg_tokens[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
            printf -v _kp_payload '%s\n' "${_cfg_tokens[@]}"
            _kp_payload="${_kp_payload%$'\n'}"
        fi
        {
            [[ -d "${_KP_CACHE_FILE%/*}" ]] || mkdir -p "${_KP_CACHE_FILE%/*}"
            printf '%s\n%s' "$_kp_key" "$_kp_payload" > "$_KP_CACHE_FILE.$$" &&
                mv -f -T "$_KP_CACHE_FILE.$$" "$_KP_CACHE_FILE"
        } 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$_KP_CACHE_FILE.$$" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi
[[ "${_cfg_tokens[0]-}" == "true" ]] && exit 0

THRESHOLD="${_cfg_tokens[1]-DEFAULT}"
[[ "$THRESHOLD" == "null" || -z "$THRESHOLD" ]] && THRESHOLD=100
# Validate threshold is a positive integer; default to 100 on parse failure.
[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-7: state-aggregate cache — mode decision (header note).
# _kp7_blen: byte length of $1 into _kp7_len (locale-proof: ${#} counts
# characters under multibyte locales; the local LC_ALL=C scope makes it
# count bytes without disturbing the ambient locale of jq/awk children).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_kp7_blen() { local LC_ALL=C; _kp7_len=${#1}; }

_KP7_CACHE="$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg"
# Size gate: below this many bytes the ORIGINAL full-scan path is already
# cheaper than the cache machinery's fixed cost (warm jq compile + post-stat
# + atomic mv ≈ 7ms vs ~4.7ms of scan per 1000 entries — measured crossover
# ≈ 1300 entries ≈ 260KB, where the gate sits). Below the gate NO cache is
# written; a valid existing cache is still honored — and since cache writes
# only happen at ≥ gate, offset ≥ gate ⇒ any warm-eligible file is above the
# gate too (no serve-without-write loop). The env override exists for the
# test harness (do not mix gate values against one state file); same trust
# class as KARPATHY_TASK_STATE (hook is warn-only, non-blocking).
_KP7_MIN="${KARPATHY_STATE_CACHE_MIN:-262144}"
[[ "$_KP7_MIN" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || _KP7_MIN=262144
_kp7_mode="cold"        # cold | fast | delta
_kp7_sum_mode="original" # original | fast | delta
_kp7_write_ok=0          # may attempt a cache write post-append
_kp7_warm=0              # 1 = primary fields sourced from the warm jq
_kp7_dev=""; _kp7_ino=""; _kp7_s0=""; _kp7_mt=""
_kp7_off=""; _kp7_bpois=""; _kp7_bnl=""; _kp7_bsum=""; _kp7_bcount=""
_kp7_bset=""; _kp7_tok=""; _kp7_toklen=0; _kp7_tail_from=1
_kp7_wcount=""; _kp7_snext=""; _kp7_pois2=""; _kp7_nls=""; _kp7_dlen=""
_kp7_endsnl=""; _kp7_allstr=""
_kp7_abs="$TASK_STATE"
[[ "$_kp7_abs" != /* ]] && _kp7_abs="$PWD/$_kp7_abs"

# awk/tail absence would make a FAST hit diverge from the old
# `awk … || echo 0` fallback (cached sum vs 0) — disable the whole feature.
if command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v tail >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _kp7_write_ok=1
    # _kp7_pre was captured by the combined stat above (config-cache block).
    if [[ -n "$_kp7_pre" ]]; then
        IFS='|' read -r _kp7_dev _kp7_ino _kp7_s0 _kp7_mt <<< "$_kp7_pre"
    elif [[ -e "$TASK_STATE" ]]; then
        _kp7_write_ok=0   # exists but stat failed (non-GNU stat) → fail open
    else
        _kp7_s0=0         # absent: cold with empty base; cacheable post-append
    fi
    if [[ "$_kp7_write_ok" -eq 1 && -n "$_kp7_dev" && -f "$TASK_STATE" && -r "$TASK_STATE" && -f "$_KP7_CACHE" ]]; then
        # Nine line-reads from ONE fd (no herestring temp file; a concurrent
        # cache mv cannot tear the read — the fd pins the inode). Line 9
        # (the set) is slurped with read -rd '' and must contain no newline
        # (exactly-9-lines shape check). Any read failure leaves fields
        # empty and the validation below falls through to cold.
        _kp7_c0=""; _kp7_c2=""; _kp7_c8=""
        _kp7_off=""; _kp7_bpois=""; _kp7_bnl=""; _kp7_bsum=""
        _kp7_bcount=""; _kp7_tok=""
        {
            IFS= read -r _kp7_c0 && IFS= read -r _kp7_off &&
            IFS= read -r _kp7_c2 && IFS= read -r _kp7_bpois &&
            IFS= read -r _kp7_bnl && IFS= read -r _kp7_bsum &&
            IFS= read -r _kp7_bcount && IFS= read -r _kp7_tok &&
            { IFS= read -rd '' _kp7_c8 || [[ -n "$_kp7_c8" ]]; }
        } 2>/dev/null < "$_KP7_CACHE" || _kp7_c0=""
        _kp7_bset="$_kp7_c8"
        _kp7_blen "$_kp7_tok"; _kp7_toklen="$_kp7_len"
        if [[ "$_kp7_c0" == "${_kp7_dev}:${_kp7_ino}:${_kp7_abs}" &&
              "$_kp7_off" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
              "$_kp7_bpois" =~ ^[01]$ &&
              "$_kp7_bnl" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
              "$_kp7_bsum" =~ ^-?[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
              "$_kp7_bcount" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
              "$_kp7_bset" == \[*\] && "$_kp7_bset" != *$'\n'* &&
              "$_kp7_toklen" -ge 1 && "$_kp7_toklen" -le 1024 &&
              "$_kp7_off" -gt "$_kp7_toklen" ]]; then
            if [[ "$_kp7_s0" == "$_kp7_off" && "$_kp7_mt" == "$_kp7_c2" ]]; then
                _kp7_mode="fast"
            elif [[ "$_kp7_s0" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_kp7_s0" -gt "$_kp7_off" ]]; then
                _kp7_mode="delta"
                _kp7_tail_from=$((_kp7_off - _kp7_toklen))
            fi
        fi
    fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WARM paths (fast/delta): one jq computes the payload fields with the
# ORIGINAL expressions plus the state aggregates from cached base + delta.
# Output: 15 NUL-chunks + in-band jq rc. Chunk 8 == "1" flags an anomaly
# (token mismatch / U+FFFD in delta / corrupt cached set): payload fields
# stay valid, aggregates are recomputed by the aux jq below (full rescan).
# The set is parsed/re-serialized ONLY when the current file is not yet a
# member or the delta carried new files (header note: membership shortcut);
# chunk 10 is "=" when the set line is byte-unchanged.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$_kp7_mode" == "fast" || "$_kp7_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
    _KP7_WARM_PROG='
        def denul($z): . / $z | join("");
        def scap($z): denul($z) | sub("\n+$"; "");
        def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
        def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
                then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
                else 1 end;
        ([0] | implode) as $z |
        try (
          (map(.tool_name // empty | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | join("\n") | scap($z)) as $tn |
          now as $now |
          ($sid | if . == "" then $user + "-" + ($now | gmtime | strftime("%Y%m%d")) else . end) as $session |
          (if $tn == "Write"
           then (map(.tool_input.content // empty) | map(if type == "string" then slines else jl end) | add // 0)
           elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit")
           then (map(.tool_input.new_string // empty) | map(if type == "string" then slines else jl end) | add // 0)
           else 0 end) as $lines |
          (if ($tn == "Write" or $tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit")
           then (map((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end)) | join("\n") | scap($z))
           else "" end) as $file |
          (if $fast == "1" then 0
           elif ($d | contains("�")) then 1
           elif (($d | startswith($tok + "\n")) | not) then 1
           else 0 end) as $anomA |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $fast == "1" then "" else $d[(($tok | length) + 1):] end) as $delta |
          ($delta | split("\n")) as $dsplit |
          (if $anomA == 1 then null
           else (try ($dsplit | map(select(length > 0) | fromjson) | [.[].file // empty]) catch null) end) as $dfiles |
          (if $anomA == 1 then 1 elif ($bpois == "1" or $dfiles == null) then 1 else 0 end) as $pois2 |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $pois2 == 1 then false
           elif ($dfiles | length) > 0 then false
           else (("," + ($bset | .[1:(length - 1)]) + ",")
                 | contains("," + ($file | tojson) + ",")) end) as $hit |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $pois2 == 1 or $hit then null
           else (try ($bset | fromjson) catch null) end) as $bs |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $pois2 == 1 or $hit then $anomA
           elif ($bs | type) != "array" then 1
           else $anomA end) as $anom |
          (if $anom == 1 or $pois2 == 1 or $hit then []
           else (($bs + $dfiles + [$file]) | unique) end) as $snext |
          (if $anom == 1 then "0"
           elif $pois2 == 1 then "0"
           elif $hit then $bcount
           else ($snext | length | tostring) end) as $files_mod |
          (if $anom == 1 then "0"
           elif $pois2 == 1 or $hit then $bcount
           else ($snext | length | tostring) end) as $count_next |
          (if $anom == 1 then ""
           elif $pois2 == 1 or $hit then "="
           else ($snext | tojson) end) as $setout |
          (if $anom == 1 then 0
           else (($bnl | tonumber)
                 + (if $delta == "" then 0 else (($dsplit | length) - 1) end)) end) as $nls |
          (if $anom == 1 then "0" else (($nls + 1) | tostring) end) as $tool_calls |
          ([$tn, ($lines | tostring), ($now | todate), ($file | tojson),
            ($session | tojson), $files_mod, $tool_calls,
            (if $anom == 1 then "1" else "0" end),
            $count_next,
            $setout,
            ($pois2 | tostring),
            ($nls | tostring),
            (if $anom == 1 then "0" else ($delta | utf8bytelength | tostring) end),
            (if $anom == 1 then "0" elif ($delta == "" or ($delta | endswith("\n"))) then "1" else "0" end),
            (if $anom == 1 then "0"
             elif $pois2 == 1 or $hit then "1"
             else (if ($snext | all(type == "string")) then "1" else "0" end) end)]
           | join($z) + $z)
        ) catch ("__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" + $z)
    '
    if [[ "$_kp7_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
        mapfile -d '' -t _kw < <(
            { _wrc=0
              jq -sj --rawfile d <(tail -c +"$_kp7_tail_from" -- "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) \
                 --arg fast "0" --arg tok "$_kp7_tok" --arg bset "$_kp7_bset" \
                 --arg bpois "$_kp7_bpois" --arg bnl "$_kp7_bnl" --arg bcount "$_kp7_bcount" \
                 --arg sid "${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}" --arg user "${USER:-unknown}" \
                 "$_KP7_WARM_PROG" 2>/dev/null || _wrc=$?
              printf '%s' "$_wrc"
            }
        )
    else

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

     3	# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
     4	# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in

    11	#
    12	# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
    13	# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
    14	# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
    15	_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    17	if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then

    20	fi
    21	unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)

Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:

- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.

**Accepted false positives (quote-blindness residue, cycle-120 C-D3)**: the inert-carrier scrub redacts a known data carrier's value (git commit `-m`, `br`/`bd -d`, `gh … create --body/--title`, `echo`/`printf`) only when the value holds **neither `$(` nor a backtick**. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
     4	# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
     5	#
     6	# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
     7	# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
     8	# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
     9	# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
    10	# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
    11	# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    19	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    20	    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    21	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    22	    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    23	    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    24	    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    25	    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    26	    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    27	    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    28	    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    29	    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    30	    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    31	    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    32	    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    33	    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    34	    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
    35	}
    36	
    37	# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
    38	checkpoint() {
    39	    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
    40	        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
    41	          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
    42	        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    43	}
    44	
    45	# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
    46	write_lines() {
    47	    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    48	    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    49	    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
    50	        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
    51	        | bash "$HOOK"
    52	}
    53	
    54	@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
    55	    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
    56	    write_lines 3
    57	    write_lines 2
    58	    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
    59	    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
    60	    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb
    61	    write_lines 2
    62	    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-bbb" ]
    63	    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
    64	    [ "$(jq -r '.over' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "false" ]
    65	    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl")" -eq 2 ]
    66	    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-bbb.jsonl")" -eq 1 ]
    67	    [ "$(tail -1 "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl" | jq -r '.running_total')" = "5" ]
    68	}
    69	
    70	@test "KS-2 with no run in progress the key is the payload's session id, then LOA_SESSION_ID" {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-098 Sprint 6C).
#
# At session start, identify the current operator (via git config user.email
# → OPERATORS.md slug match), then surface any unread L6 handoffs addressed
# to them. Body content is sanitized via context-isolation-lib's
# sanitize_for_session_start("L6", body) before reaching session context.
#
# This hook is silent (exit 0 with no stdout) when:
#   - structured_handoff.enabled is not true in .loa.config.yaml
#   - operator slug cannot be resolved (no git config user.email match)
#   - no unread handoffs for this operator
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
LIB="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/structured-handoff-lib.sh"
[[ -f "$LIB" ]] || exit 0

# Gate on config.
if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    enabled="false"
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
        enabled="$(loa_knob structured_handoff.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
else
    # No config → silent (the primitive is opt-in).
    exit 0
fi

# Resolve current operator slug from git config.
git_email="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" config user.email 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
[[ -n "$git_email" ]] || exit 0

# Source operator-identity to map email → slug. Fall back: skip surfacing.
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
LIB="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/soul-identity-lib.sh"
[[ -f "$LIB" ]] || exit 0

# Cache scoped to session — re-source no-ops (FR-L7-5).
[[ "${LOA_L7_SURFACED:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 0

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test-mode env-gated path overrides (LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG +
# LOA_SOUL_TEST_PATH). Honored ONLY under bats / LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE=1 with a
# bats-detected ancestor. Mirrors L4/L6 cycle-098 patterns.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
_l7_test_mode_active() {
    # cycle-098 sprint-7 cypherpunk CRIT-1 remediation: require BOTH a
    # robust bats marker AND opt-in `LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE=1`. Mirrors the
    # lib-side gate at .claude/scripts/lib/soul-identity-lib.sh.
    [[ "${LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
    [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
    [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
if _l7_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG:-}" ]]; then
    config_path="$LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG"
fi

# Gate on yq availability + config presence.
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$config_path" ]] || exit 0

# Read enable / mode / max-chars / path keys. Silent on malformed YAML
# (each yq returns the default).
# The enable key: explicit, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
enabled="false"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
if source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null; then
    if [[ "$config_path" != "${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
        enabled="$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$config_path" loa_knob soul_identity_doc.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    else
        enabled="$(loa_knob soul_identity_doc.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    fi
fi
[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0

schema_mode="$(yq '.soul_identity_doc.schema_mode // "warn"' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || echo warn)"
case "$schema_mode" in
    strict|warn) ;;

export PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH
CK=$HOME/rc/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh
newrepo() {

}
feedback() {
  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
  else prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'; fi

    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
}
complete() { feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"; feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"; printf 'COMPLETED x\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"; }
cache() {
  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", state: $s,

}
d() { bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
EOF
echo ok

All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

### Red Team Code-vs-Design Circuit Breaker

Separate counter from the main circuit breaker (see `resources/conditional-procedures.md`
§red-team-code-gate for behavior).

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  local v
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}
cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
# previous file is untouched.
atomic_update() {
  local f="$1"; shift
  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
  (
    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
    else
      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
    fi
    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
  return $rc
}

All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

### Red Team Code-vs-Design Circuit Breaker

Separate counter from the main circuit breaker (see `resources/conditional-procedures.md`
§red-team-code-gate for behavior).

I found five defects I'm confident in, plus two weaker issues. I checked the profile-lib items by running the head `profile-lib.sh` in a scratch copy; the `PL-1`..`PL-13` tests pass there against a stub `floor.yaml` I wrote, since the PR doesn't include that file.

### Confirmed defects

**1. head/.loa.config.yaml.example:21 and :33 — `loa.profile` has almost no effect for anyone who starts from the shipped example.** Confidence: high.
- The comment at :21 says "`lean` turns them all off, `full` all on". But the example also sets 8 of the 9 profile keys explicitly, at :312, :325, :1358, :1404, :1432, :2932, :2950 and :2962. Explicit keys win over the profile.
- Repro: copy the example, set `loa.profile: full`, run `profile-lib.sh json`. Only `soul_identity_doc.enabled` changes. Guardrails, the decisions and KF surfaces, and handoffs stay `false`, and `overrides` reports five "explicit overrides" the user never chose. `lean` has the same problem.
- `PL-4` (head/tests/unit/profile-lib.bats:76-78) asserts empty overrides under the example, so the test locks this in.

**2. head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77-78 — the cache key ignores file changes on Linux whenever any of the three inputs is missing.** Confidence: high (reproduced).
- GNU `stat -Lc` exits 1 if any operand is missing (e.g. no `.loa.config.yaml`, or no `floor.yaml`). The `||` fallback then runs `stat -Lf`, which on GNU means "file-system status", not BSD format.
- The key is then built from disk free-block and inode counts instead of mtimes. The `id` in my repro contained `Type: tmpfs; Blocks: ... Free: 261475`.
- Repro (scratch root, no `floor.yaml`): rewrite the config in place `full` → `lean` → `full`. `knob soul_identity_doc.enabled` returned `false` each time; with `floor.yaml` present it correctly returned true/false/true.
- So the cache can serve stale values, or rebuild on almost every call. The comment at :73-74 ("empty stat output … disables caching") doesn't describe this path.

**3. head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:208 (`_loa_pl_live`) — an explicitly set key reads as the fallback when `jq` is not installed.** Confidence: high on the mechanism, medium on real-world impact.
- `_loa_pl_load` needs jq, and the live-read fallback also needs jq, so with yq but no jq every key returns the fallback. Verified: a config with `known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true` printed `false`.
- The base hooks only needed yq. Affected:
  - `head/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh:62-64` and `head/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-l7-surface-soul.sh:67-74`: an explicit `true` is now silently ignored. Neither hook uses jq anywhere else.
  - `head/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh:50-51`: this breaks the hook's own contract (header lines 11-12). An enabled surface with jq missing should print the "[DECISIONS] WARNING … jq is missing" line; now it prints nothing.

**4. head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:61-65 — the config seams are honoured in production, not only under bats.** Confidence: medium-high.
- `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILES_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_ROOT` and `LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE` are read unconditionally. Only `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` is bats-gated (:58-60).
- The lib is now sourced by the L6/L7 surfacing hooks, `danger-level-enforcer.sh:138` and `guardrails-orchestrator.sh:107`. So one environment variable can switch danger-level enforcement or the input guardrails off, or turn L7 surfacing on.
- That bypasses the hooks' own two-factor test gates (L7 header: "cypherpunk CRIT-1 remediation"). It also contradicts the kernel invariant in CLAUDE.loa.md: "test-mode env overrides are test-mode/bats gated". `PL-15`/`PL-16` depend on the ungated seam.

**5. head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42 — `standard` quietly turns `invisible_retrospective.enabled` on for every config that doesn't set the key, including this repository's own.** Confidence: medium.
- The base postlude ran the scan only on an explicit `true`. The oracle records `this_repo_today: false` and `empty_config_today: false` (head/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json, `invisible_retrospective.enabled` entry), and head `.loa.config.yaml` doesn't set the key.
- So the silent post-skill scan is now on by default. The profiles.yaml header (:14-15) lists only the two guardrail keys as default changes.
- Smaller related point: the include `head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` calls `knob` with no fallback (empty), while `continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34` documents a fallback of `true`.

### Lower-confidence issues

- **head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257 and :320 — the exit-code test was weakened.** The "exit 0 = all pass (good fixture)" check now accepts exit 1 (`assert_no_errors_exit`), so nothing tests the exit-0 path any more.
- **head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:124 — the floor match only half-covers what the header (:36-38) promises.** The ancestor check uses only the text before the first `*`: `flatline_protocol.code_review` is not caught as an ancestor of `flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice`, and a descendant of an exact floor key (e.g. `hounfour.locality.x`) isn't caught either. `PF-2` (head/tests/unit/profile-floor.bats:56-57) has the same gap. Today nothing reads a floor key through `loa_knob`, so it can't be exploited yet.

### Checked, no defect found

- generate-constraints pruning (`prune_optional_table`) and the matching `lint-invariants` check (4b).
- The validate-constraints sections and the C-TEAM rules moving into agent-teams-reference.md (the IDR-3 parsing works).
- The keep-list K-07 regex and the `^## Rules and arming$` heading.
- The prompt budget: CLAUDE.loa.md is 9,189 B against the 9,445 B cap.
- The pure-review strip validator (yq expression tested on list, string and empty forms) and the `rtfm-testing` exception.
- The `check-knob-readers.sh` pattern.
- The `run-checkpoint` subcommands referenced in the SKILL.md prose.

I couldn't verify anything that needs files outside the PR, such as the real `floor.yaml`, `guard-origins.bats` or the `prompt-budget` fixtures.

Six defects confirmed, five of them reproduced. The new implement-gate tests (IG-11, IG-24 to IG-33) and the karpathy tests pass in a scratch copy at /tmp/ig, so none of the issues below is caught by the suite. The older implement-gate tests that failed there were missing fixtures that aren't in the frozen PR. KS-11 failed only because /tmp is mounted noexec.

**1. head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:505 (with :564, :629): deny mode refuses writes while the derived run position says RUNNING.** Confidence: high, reproduced.
- The run sanction checks `last_activity` against a fixed 24 h (`_ig_fresh`, :470).
- `read_position` decides the position is "known" using `run_mode.stale_hours`, which the config accepts up to 8760 (:202). `run-checkpoint.sh derive` also uses `stale_hours` to decide RUNNING.
- Repro: `mode: deny`, `stale_hours: 48`, sprint-plan cache `{plan_id, state: RUNNING, derived_at: now, last_activity: now-30h}`. Output is `permissionDecision: deny`, "no active implementation run (derived position: RUNNING)", with a `deny/deny` row. The message contradicts itself and a legitimate run is fenced.

**2. head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:510: regression against base.** Confidence: high, reproduced.
- The new `_ig_derived_ok` check returns 1 before the `state == RUNNING` test. A non-RUNNING sprint-plan cache with an old `derived_at` therefore stops the function from ever checking `simstim-state.json` or `state.json`.
- Repro: sprint-plan `{plan_id, state: COMPLETE, derived_at: now-13h, last_activity: now}` plus `simstim-state.json {phase: implementation, last_activity: now}`. Base allows the write; head asks.
- This contradicts hooks-reference.md:248, "The legacy state files below keep sanctioning as before". The failure is towards asking, not allowing.

**3. head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:129-137: the key never falls back to the session after any run has finished.** Confidence: high, reproduced.
- The task key comes from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`, with no check of the run state or the checkpoint age. A finished run leaves `sprint-plan-state.json` behind with its last checkpoint.
- Repro: cache `{state: JACKED_OUT, checkpoint: {task: bd-old, ts: 2026-01-01}}`, then two writes from sessions `sessA` and `sessB`. Both go to `bd-old.jsonl`, the total grows to 6 lines and the warning fires.
- So every later session adds to a stale task's total indefinitely. That is the session-long growth this rework was meant to remove, and it contradicts the header's "else the session id" (:11-13).

**4. head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:10 (key logic at :132): totals are credited to the previous task.** Confidence: high, from the specs.
- The header says the key is "the current task". But `checkpoint.task` is "the last CLOSED bead" (state-schemas.md:107).
- `read` only trusts a task checkpoint once beads confirms the task is closed, and implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:211 writes the checkpoint after `br close`.
- So lines written for task N+1 accumulate under task N, and the summary's `task` (read by the review's SURGICAL axis) names the wrong task. Test KS-1 fakes this with a closed bead and never checks the real ordering.

**5. head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550: the two-hour marker is never refreshed, so a long /implement gets denied under deny mode.** Confidence: medium; this is design-level.
- `mark` runs once, at the start of the skill. It also runs `derive --write` whenever a sprint-plan cache exists, which stamps a fresh `derived_at` and makes the position "known" for 12 h.
- With a leftover cache (COMPLETE or JACKED_OUT), a direct `/implement` that runs longer than 2 h therefore gets `deny` on its own App Zone writes for the rest of that window.

**6. head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:271: the docs don't match the claim rows.** Confidence: medium.
- The docs say each decision row carries `hook`, `action`, `decision` and `mode`.
- The claim ask/deny decision rows (implement-gate.sh:423-424) set `mode: "authoritative"` and put the real gate mode under `gate_mode`. They, and the trust-input row (:349), use `timestamp` and a raw `file_path`, not `ts` and the stripped `path`.
- Anything grouping by `.mode` or `.ts` will put these rows in the wrong bucket or drop them. I couldn't check `guard-yield.sh`'s parser because it isn't part of the PR.

**Test gap (minor):** in head/tests/unit/implement-gate.bats, the "mode × claims" matrix in `gate_cell` only ever sends a non-implementation claim (`review-sprint`). An implementation claim, which falls through to the mode logic, is not tested in any mode.

The guard-origins.yaml notes match the hooks-reference rows exactly, and the "33 cases" count is correct.

content.text:
I found 9 defects in the run-position code, two docs and two tests, with line numbers in the pr/head files. All but #9 I reproduced in a scratch copy (`$HOME/rc`) using bats 1.13. The repo's `verdict-derive.sh` isn't in the PR snapshot, so I stubbed it there to parse the trailer, and I used a downloaded jq 1.7.1 next to the system jq 1.6.

With jq 1.7.1 and the stub, all 8 RCR tests and RCD-1…17 pass. RCD-R1/R2/R3 fail only because files outside the PR are missing. RCD-R5 needed a `workflow-state.sh` stub and an exec-capable temp dir, and then passed.

**1. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:380 (also 378, 389) — `derive` does not run at all on jq 1.6.** (High confidence)
- `$label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6, which fails with "syntax error, unexpected label"; jq 1.7 accepts it.
- Because the fix is a variable rename, this is a regression the PR introduced.
- Effect: `derive` exits 3 every time. Every `write` and `mark` also prints jq errors and a misleading "sprint-plan-state.json is not valid JSON — not written" while still exiting 0, and leaves a stray breaker file behind.
- jq 1.6 is still the default on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 11. Renaming the variable (e.g. `$lbl`) fixes it.

**2. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226 (same pattern at 223) — on jq 1.6, `record-round` crashes on feedback files without a trailer.** (High confidence on jq 1.6)
- jq 1.6's `jq -e` returns 0 on empty input (1.7 returns 4), so the empty trailer text passes the check.
- It then reaches `--argjson p ""` at line 232, which fails with "invalid JSON text passed to --argjson", so `record-round` exits 2.
- RCR-7 fails on jq 1.6 and passes on 1.7.1.

**3. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:154 + 295 (called from 456) — `derive --write` with no breaker file creates a broken breaker.** (High confidence)
- `atomic_update` feeds `{}` when the file is missing, and `merge_breaker` treats any object as an existing breaker, so the default skeleton is never applied.
- The file written is only `{"triggers":{"cycle_count":{"current":0}},"state":"CLOSED"}`: no thresholds or limits, no `timeout.started`, no `history`.
- A later `record-round` keeps it, because `.triggers` is an object. It then prints `cycle 1/null, same_issue 1/null, no_progress 0/null`, and the timeout trigger can never fire because `started` is null.
- This contradicts the header (line 76: defaults "for a new breaker file").
- `derive --json` uses `null` and so shows the proper skeleton: the report and the file that gets written disagree.

**4. head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:69-72, 84-86 vs head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:324 — `/run-resume --force` without `--reset-ice` is undone by the next checkpoint.** (Medium-high confidence)
- The doc offers `--force` as "continue without reset (may halt again)" and says step 3's RUNNING clears the sticky HALTED.
- But `resolve` returns HALTED whenever the breaker is OPEN, and every `write` runs `derive --write`.
- Reproduced: breaker OPEN, cache RUNNING, one `write` → sprint-plan-state.json becomes `{"state":"HALTED","status":"HALTED"}`. A forced resume halts again immediately.

**5. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:50 vs 456/459 — `derive` exit codes are wrong in the docs, and a corrupt breaker blocks every state rewrite.** (High confidence)
- The header lists `derive` exits as only 0, 4 and 2, but `--write` returns 3.
- Reproduced: with `circuit-breaker.json` containing `{bad`, `derive --write` exits 3 and sprint-plan-state.json is never rewritten (stays RUNNING while the files say COMPLETE).
- Meanwhile `derive --json` reports the breaker as `CLOSED` from the skeleton, so the report fails open.

**6. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:497-504 (and recompute 284-285) — no_progress trips on trailerless (legacy) feedback even when the findings change.** (Medium confidence)
- `counts` is null for legacy files, so `tojson` gives the string "null" every round and every round compares equal.
- Reproduced: 6 legacy rounds with different findings → same_issue stays 1, yet the breaker reports `TRIPPED: no_progress: finding counts unchanged for 5 consecutive rounds` and exits 10.

**7. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:278 — once any `reset_at` exists, rounds without a trailer `ts` are always dropped.** (Medium confidence, low severity)
- The filter `(.ts // "") > $reset` is false for a missing ts, so those rounds are excluded whether they came before or after the reset.
- The header (lines 40-41) and state-schemas.md say only rounds *before* `reset_at` are ignored.
- Reproduced: 2 legacy `-rN` rounds recompute to cycle 2, and to 0 after any `reset_at`.

**8. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:411-414 vs 456 — race with `/run-resume --reset-ice`.** (Medium confidence, narrow window)
- `reset_at` and the recomputed counters (`rc`) are read outside the breaker lock, then merged under the lock at line 456.
- The reset in halt-resume.md:81 is a plain jq → `.tmp` → `mv` that doesn't take the lock.
- If it lands between those two points, `merge_breaker` raises the zeroed counters back from the full history and re-trips OPEN, silently undoing the reset.

**9. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:463 — "schema_version kept" isn't quite true.** (High confidence it happens, low severity; not reproduced, read from the code and the RCD-11 assertion)
- `.schema_version // 2` stamps 2 on files that have no `schema_version`, which readers treat as version 1 (lines 191 and 73).

The repo's `verdict-derive.sh` isn't in the PR snapshot, so I stubbed it there to parse the trailer, and I used a downloaded jq 1.7.1 next to the system jq 1.6.

With jq 1.7.1 and the stub, all 8 RCR tests and RCD-1…17 pass. RCD-R1/R2/R3 fail only because files outside the PR are missing. RCD-R5 needed a `workflow-state.sh` stub and an exec-capable temp dir, and then passed.

**1. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:380 (also 378, 389) — `derive` does not run at all on jq 1.6.** (High confidence)
- `$label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6, which fails with "syntax error, unexpected label"; jq 1.7 accepts it.
- Because the fix is a variable rename, this is a regression the PR introduced.
- Effect: `derive` exits 3 every time. Every `write` and `mark` also prints jq errors and a misleading "sprint-plan-state.json is not valid JSON — not written" while still exiting 0, and leaves a stray breaker file behind.
- jq 1.6 is still the default on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 11. Renaming the variable (e.g. `$lbl`) fixes it.

**2. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226 (same pattern at 223) — on jq 1.6, `record-round` crashes on feedback files without a trailer.** (High confidence on jq 1.6)
- jq 1.6's `jq -e` returns 0 on empty input (1.7 returns 4), so the empty trailer text passes the check.
- It then reaches `--argjson p ""` at line 232, which fails with "invalid JSON text passed to --argjson", so `record-round` exits 2.
- RCR-7 fails on jq 1.6 and passes on 1.7.1.

**3. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:154 + 295 (called from 456) — `derive --write` with no breaker file creates a broken breaker.** (High confidence)
- `atomic_update` feeds `{}` when the file is missing, and `merge_breaker` treats any object as an existing breaker, so the default skeleton is never applied.
- The file written is only `{"triggers":{"cycle_count":{"current":0}},"state":"CLOSED"}`: no thresholds or limits, no `timeout.started`, no `history`.
- A later `record-round` keeps it, because `.triggers` is an object. It then prints `cycle 1/null, same_issue 1/null, no_progress 0/null`, and the timeout trigger can never fire because `started` is null.
- This contradicts the header (line 76: defaults "for a new breaker file").
- `derive --json` uses `null` and so shows the proper skeleton: the report and the file that gets written disagree.

**4. head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:69-72, 84-86 vs head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:324 — `/run-resume --force` without `--reset-ice` is undone by the next checkpoint.** (Medium-high confidence)

- But `resolve` returns HALTED whenever the breaker is OPEN, and every `write` runs `derive --write`.
- Reproduced: breaker OPEN, cache RUNNING, one `write` → sprint-plan-state.json becomes `{"state":"HALTED","status":"HALTED"}`. A forced resume halts again immediately.

**5. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:50 vs 456/459 — `derive` exit codes are wrong in the docs, and a corrupt breaker blocks every state rewrite.** (High confidence)
- The header lists `derive` exits as only 0, 4 and 2, but `--write` returns 3.
- Reproduced: with `circuit-breaker.json` containing `{bad`, `derive --write` exits 3 and sprint-plan-state.json is never rewritten (stays RUNNING while the files say COMPLETE).
- Meanwhile `derive --json` reports the breaker as `CLOSED` from the skeleton, so the report fails open.

**6. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:497-504 (and recompute 284-285) — no_progress trips on trailerless (legacy) feedback even when the findings change.** (Medium confidence)
- `counts` is null for legacy files, so `tojson` gives the string "null" every round and every round compares equal.
- Reproduced: 6 legacy rounds with different findings → same_issue stays 1, yet the breaker reports `TRIPPED: no_progress: finding counts unchanged for 5 consecutive rounds` and exits 10.

**7. head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:278 — once any `reset_at` exists, rounds without a trailer `ts` are always dropped.** (Medium confidence, low severity)
- The filter `(.ts // "") > $reset` is false for a missing ts, so those rounds are excluded whether they came before or after the reset.

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:631 — FR-6 bypass (fail-open regression): _bdb_hd_same_line_exec only flags a segment whose token *is* the target's basename and whose command word is not a safe reader, so `cat > cmds.txt <<'EOF' … EOF` followed on the same command by `cat cmds.txt | bash` (cat is a "safe reader", bash has no target token) or `bash -c "$(cat cmds.txt)"` (basename buried inside a substitution token) is classed nonexec. The body is reduced to fence-verb segments, so e.g. `echo pwn > .claude/hooks/x.sh` / `> .run/cron.d/job` are dropped from the scan. Reproduced: the base hook blocks (FR-SZ2-REDIR / FR-SZ-REDIR, exit 2), the head hook allows (exit 0). A "fail-closed" classifier has to treat any line that pipes or substitutes a target into an interpreter as interpreter-class.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303 — _bdb_hd_exec_dest only knows script extensions, hook, rc and PATH locations, so files that a later word on the same command runs implicitly count as plain data. Example: `cat > Makefile <<'EOF'` with recipe `echo pwn > .claude/hooks/x.sh`, then `make`. Base blocks, head allows (reproduced). package.json/justfile/Taskfile with npm/just/task fail the same way. This is a same-command case, not the "later command" gap the header documents.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:380 — `--arg label`/`$label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6 ("syntax error, unexpected label"; reproduced with the system jq-1.6). On jq 1.6 `derive` always exits 3, and every `write`/`mark` (which runs `derive --write`) prints jq errors and a misleading "not valid JSON — not written". Rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`), also at lines 378/389.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226 — the trailer check relies on `jq -e` failing on empty input, which only jq ≥1.7 does. On jq 1.6 a feedback file without a verdict trailer gets through and then fails at `--argjson p ""` (line 232), so `record-round` exits 2 (RCR-7 fails on jq 1.6).
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:295 — merge_breaker treats any object as an existing breaker, but atomic_update feeds `{}` when circuit-breaker.json is missing (line 154). `derive --write` therefore writes `{"triggers":{"cycle_count":{"current":0}},"state":"CLOSED"}` with no thresholds, no timeout.started and no history. Later record-round output shows `n/null` limits and the timeout trigger can never fire. This contradicts the "defaults for a new breaker file" contract (line 76), and `derive --json` reports a different (full) skeleton than the file it writes.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:324 — resolve returns HALTED whenever the breaker is OPEN, and every checkpoint `write` re-derives. So the documented `/run-resume --force` without `--reset-ice` (halt-resume.md:69-72, 84-86: "step 3's RUNNING clears the sticky HALTED") is undone by the very next checkpoint (reproduced: cache RUNNING + breaker OPEN → one write → state HALTED).
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:456 — a corrupt circuit-breaker.json makes `derive --write` exit 3, which is not among the derive exit codes in the header (line 50: 0/4/2), and sprint-plan-state.json is never rewritten (it stays RUNNING while the files say COMPLETE). `derive --json` meanwhile reports the breaker as CLOSED from the skeleton, so the report fails open.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:497 — the no_progress comparison uses `counts | tojson`, which is "null" for every legacy (trailerless) round. Legacy rounds therefore always compare equal, and the breaker trips no_progress (exit 10) even though the findings change every round (reproduced with 6 legacy rounds).
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:278 — `(.ts // "") > $reset` is false for a round with no ts. Once any reset_at exists, every trailerless round is dropped whether it came before or after the reset. The header (lines 40-41) and state-schemas.md say only rounds before reset_at are ignored.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:411 — reset_at and the recomputed counters are read outside the breaker lock and merged under it at line 456. The `--reset-ice` reset in halt-resume.md:81 is a plain jq→tmp→mv that takes no lock. If the reset lands in that window, merge_breaker raises the zeroed counters back and re-trips OPEN, silently undoing the reset.
head/tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats:105 — RCR-5 claims the triggers "trip in that documented order", but each sub-case pushes only one trigger to its threshold. The precedence between triggers (run-checkpoint.sh:507-515) is never tested.
head/tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats:99 — RCR-4's "further round on an OPEN breaker" passes only because same_issue re-trips (4 ≥ 3). The breaker-already-OPEN branch (run-checkpoint.sh:515/520) is never exercised.
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:505 — the run sanction still requires last_activity within a fixed 24 h (_ig_fresh). The derived position and `run-checkpoint.sh derive` call a run RUNNING within run_mode.stale_hours, which accepts up to 8760. With stale_hours > 24 and mode deny, a live RUNNING run more than 24 h after its last activity is denied with the self-contradictory "no active implementation run (derived position: RUNNING)" (reproduced with stale_hours 48, last_activity now-30h).
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:510 — the new _ig_derived_ok check returns 1 from check_implementation_active before the state==RUNNING test. A non-RUNNING sprint-plan cache with an old derived_at therefore stops the simstim-state.json/state.json sanctions from being consulted. Base allowed this case (simstim phase=implementation, fresh); head asks. This contradicts hooks-reference.md:248 ("legacy state files keep sanctioning as before"). The check should only gate the sprint-plan RUNNING branch.
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550 — the /implement marker is honoured for only 2 h after started_at and nothing refreshes it. `mark` also runs `derive --write`, which stamps a fresh derived_at onto a leftover COMPLETE/JACKED_OUT cache, so the position counts as "known" for stale_hours. A direct /implement that runs longer than 2 h is then denied on its own App Zone writes under deny mode.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131 — the task key comes from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` without checking run state or checkpoint age. After any run finishes (JACKED_OUT/COMPLETE cache left behind), every later session's lines go to the stale task's ledger and keep growing its total, which is the unbounded growth this rework was meant to remove. This contradicts the header's "else the session id" (lines 11-13). Reproduced: sessions sessA and sessB both accrue to bd-old.jsonl.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:10 — the header says totals are keyed by "the current task", but checkpoint.task is the last CLOSED bead (state-schemas.md; implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:211 writes it after `br close`). Lines written for task N+1 are credited to task N, and the SURGICAL review axis reads the wrong task. KS-1 fakes the ordering with an already-closed bead.
head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:271 — the docs say decision rows carry hook/action/decision/mode. The implement-gate claim ask/deny rows (implement-gate.sh:423-424) set `mode: "authoritative"` and put the real mode under `gate_mode`, and they and the trust-input row (implement-gate.sh:349) use `timestamp` and a raw `file_path` instead of `ts`/`path`. Consumers that group by `.mode` or `.ts` mis-bucket or drop them.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77 — GNU `stat -Lc` exits 1 if any operand is missing (no floor.yaml, or no .loa.config.yaml). The `||` fallback then runs `stat -Lf`, which on GNU means filesystem status, so the cache key is built from free-block and inode counts, not mtimes. Edits to the config are then served stale (reproduced: full→lean→full returned the same value each time) or the cache rebuilds on nearly every call. Stat only the existing files, or detect GNU vs BSD up front.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:208 — both _loa_pl_load and the live-read fallback need jq. Under yq without jq, every explicitly set key returns the fallback. Before this change, loa-kf-surface.sh / loa-l7-surface-soul.sh needed only yq; an explicit `true` is now silently ignored. loa-decisions-surface.sh also loses its documented "jq is missing" warning (its header lines 11-12).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:61 — LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE / LOA_PROFILES_FILE / LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE / LOA_PROFILE_ROOT / LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE are honoured outside bats; only LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is gated (lines 58-60). The lib now feeds danger-level-enforcer.sh, guardrails-orchestrator.sh and the L6/L7 surfacing hooks, so one env var can switch off danger-level enforcement or input guardrails, or turn L7 surfacing on. That bypasses the hooks' own two-factor test gates and the kernel rule that test-mode env overrides are bats-gated.
head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42 — `standard` (the default profile) sets invisible_retrospective.enabled: true. Base ran the retrospective scan only on an explicit true. The oracle records false for this repo and for an empty config today (standard-oracle.json), and .loa.config.yaml does not set the key, so the silent post-skill scan is newly on for every user. The header (lines 14-15) lists only the two guardrail keys as default changes.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:21 — the comment says `lean` turns these keys all off and `full` all on, but the example explicitly sets 8 of the 9 profile keys (lines 312, 325, 1358, 1404, 1432, 2932, 2950, 2962), and explicit keys beat the profile. For anyone starting from the example, `loa.profile: full`/`lean` changes only soul_identity_doc.enabled and reports five "explicit overrides" the user never chose. PL-4 (profile-lib.bats:76-78) locks this in.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
